author: Xtra Demo Desk
subject: Welcome to the local newsgroups
body:
Welcome aboard. General chat in xtra.general, practical questions in
xtra.help, old hardware in xtra.retro. Try xtra.test if you are still
getting the hang of your reader.

Plain text preferred. Trim your quotes and let us know when a fix works.
Announcements are read only; discussion belongs in the other groups.

author: Mara Packet
subject: GUIDE: reading news without staying online
body:
1. Add the news server 10.150.150.157, port 119.
2. Leave SSL and news-server authentication off on this private service.
3. Fetch the group list and subscribe to xtra.general and xtra.help.
4. Download message bodies before disconnecting, if your reader supports it.
5. Read offline. Compose replies, then reconnect to send them.

Downloading only headers does not necessarily save the articles for offline
reading. Check your reader's download/synchronise options.

Your display name and From address are visible to everyone reading a post.
Use xtra.test to check your setup. There is no public Usenet feed here.

author: Kev Baud
subject: Re: GUIDE: reading news without staying online
body:
> Download message bodies before disconnecting.

I downloaded only the subjects and spent the evening imagining the answers.
Excellent compression, although the technical accuracy was variable.

author: Mara Packet
subject: Re: GUIDE: reading news without staying online
body:
That is an advanced feature called speculation. For actual answers, ask
for complete articles rather than headers before hanging up. :)

author: Ruth Handshake
subject: GUIDE: CONNECT speed is not download speed
body:
A 33,600 bit/s modem connection is not a 33,600 byte/s download.
Divide bits by eight first: 4,200 bytes/s before protocol overhead.
Actual file transfer will usually be lower. Line conditions, retries and
the remote server all matter; compressed files rarely compress much more.

For a useful comparison, time a reasonably sized local ZIP download.
Write down the negotiated modem rate and the bytes actually transferred.
A second multilink modem adds capacity only while both links are working.

Do not change several modem settings at once. Keep notes so you can undo
an experiment. Please include your modem model when asking for help.

author: Glen Buffer
subject: 33.6 modem, downloads around 3 KB/sec. Faulty?
body:
My modem says CONNECT 33600 but the browser says about 3 KB/sec. I expected
33.6 KB/sec. Have I purchased the economy version of the Internet?

Machine is a Pentium 100 with 16 MB and a very determined hard drive.

author: Ruth Handshake
subject: Re: 33.6 modem, downloads around 3 KB/sec. Faulty?
body:
That sounds plausible for a 33.6 kbit/s link. See the CONNECT-speed guide.
The connection rate is in bits; your browser is reporting bytes.
Try a local ZIP download before changing any modem settings.

author: Kev Baud
subject: Re: 33.6 modem, downloads around 3 KB/sec. Faulty?
body:
Have you tried holding the mouse closer to the modem? Shorter route for
the packets. No, I have not measured this. Yes, I am being told to stop.

author: Glen Buffer
subject: Re: 33.6 modem, downloads around 3 KB/sec. Faulty?
body:
Local ZIP is roughly the same speed. The guide explains it, thanks.
Moving the mouse made no difference except knocking over my tea.

author: Nicky Retry
subject: Imaginary fault: busy tone at exactly dinner time

every time I try to dial at dinner time, somebody
in the house is already on the telephone. Is this a routing problem?

Please advise before the mashed potatoes go cold.

author: Mo Exchange
subject: Re: Imaginary fault: busy tone at exactly dinner time
body:
That is household resource contention. The usual fix is agreeing when
the line can be used. A software update cannot create a second phone line.
Do not interrupt an active call to test modem commands.

author: Kev Baud
subject: Re: Imaginary fault: busy tone at exactly dinner time
body:
Escalate to the kitchen. Ask for the duty parent. Have your washing-up
reference number ready.

author: Tessa Inbox
subject: Mail arrives in browser but not my mail program
body:
I can see a message in webmail, but my desktop
mail program has not fetched it. I put my whole email address in every
box because it seemed thorough. What should I check?

author: Mara Packet
subject: Re: Mail arrives in browser but not my mail program
body:
Check the client settings page on the mail service for the exact server,
port and username format. Do not guess SSL/port combinations. Then check
whether the client actually reports a successful fetch.

Please post the error text, but never your password or a screenshot that
shows it. The From address and login name need not have identical formats.

author: Tessa Inbox
subject: Re: Mail arrives in browser but not my mail program
body:
The ticket is resolved: I had configured the outgoing server
where the incoming server should have been. The names were in two boxes,
so statistically I had a fifty-fifty chance.

author: DJ Bitbucket
subject: GUIDE: choosing a radio stream for dial-up
body:
Radio page: http://10.150.150.157:8089/

Try the 16 kbit/s mono MP3 first. The number is the audio rate; containers
and network traffic add overhead. Leave room for whatever else you are
doing. If playback repeatedly stops, choose a lower rate or stop downloads.

8 kbit/s MP3 needs MPEG-2.5 support. WMA starts at 24 kbit/s. The RM option
is 8 kbit/s RealAudio; expect telephone-like sound, not hi-fi.
The Listen links launch an external player when the association is set.

Do not assume a 64 kbit/s stream fits a single dial-up modem.

author: Pete Cassette
subject: Re: GUIDE: choosing a radio stream for dial-up
body:
At 8 kbit/s I can no longer tell whether it is a guitar solo or my kettle.
Conveniently, I enjoy both.

author: DJ Bitbucket
subject: Re: GUIDE: choosing a radio stream for dial-up
body:
Teh kettle has a wider frequency response. Try 16 or 24 if your link has
room, and let teh initial buffer fill before judging it.

author: Jo Underconstruction
subject: GUIDE: your first personal homepage
body:
Create a small file named index.html. A heading and a paragraph will do.
Upload it by FTP to 10.150.150.157 using your personal web-space account.
Your FTP root is the public web directory; do not upload passwords there.

Browse http://10.150.150.157:8086/~yourname/ afterwards, replacing yourname
with the account name. If you use a picture, its filename and letter case
must match the HTML. The account dashboard can edit a small index.html too.

A tiny GIF is kind to dial-up callers. A 2 MB photograph of an UNDER
CONSTRUCTION sign is a philosophical contradiction.

subject: Re: GUIDE: your first personal homepage
body:

author: Jo Underconstruction
subject: Re: GUIDE: your first personal homepage
body: Please put teh actual page somewhere between teh counters.

author: Ash Jumper
subject: 16 MB or 32 MB for a Win95 box?

Mostly mail, news and staring at a browser progress bar.

author: Ruth Handshake
subject: Re: 16 MB or 32 MB for a Win95 box?
body:
If it is constantly swapping, more compatible RAM is likely to make the
machine feel better. It will not change the phone line's connection rate.
Check the motherboard manual: SIMM type, parity and pairing requirements
vary. Do not buy random sticks on optimism alone.

author: Kev Baud
subject: Re: 16 MB or 32 MB for a Win95 box?

author: Ash Jumper

idea for the marketing department.

author: Bea IRQ
subject: IRQ conflict or just a bad afternoon?

Both worked separately. I now have a computer that makes a startup sound
but cannot be persuaded to click anything. Where would you start?

author: Mo Exchange
subject: Re: IRQ conflict or just a bad afternoon?
body:
Record the cards' present jumper settings and inspect the assigned I/O
addresses and IRQs. Compare with their manuals before changing anything.
Power down before moving ISA hardware. Try one change, then retest.

The phrase "Plug and Play" is a statement of intent, not an alibi.

author: Bea IRQ
subject: Re: IRQ conflict or just a bad afternoon?
body:
in this case the card had been jumpered onto a serial-port IRQ.
Moved it to a documented free setting. Mouse has returned to management.

author: Xtra Demo Desk
subject: A short guide to being excellent on news
body:
A few requests:

Trim repeated quotes and signatures. Reply in the thread. Give your
modem model and the actual error message when asking for help.
Do not post passwords or other people's private mail.

If somebody's suggestion fixes it, say so. Nothing worse than finding
your exact problem in a thread which ends with "never mind, fixed it".

author: Fern Filename
subject: My homepage works, but the picture is missing

author: Jo Underconstruction
subject: Re: My homepage works, but the picture is missing
body:
Use the exact same spelling and letter case in the HTML and uploaded
filename. The server can distinguish LOGO.GIF from logo.gif even if your
local filesystem does not. Also check that the image is in the directory
your relative link points to. Keep a local copy before renaming files.

author: Kev Baud
subject: Re: My homepage works, but the picture is missing
body:
The picture is probably still developing. Leave the page in a dark room
for twenty minutes. This advice has not survived peer review.

author: Fern Filename
subject: Re: My homepage works, but the picture is missing
body:
Matching the case fixed this ticket. The logo is now visible
and unfortunately confirms that I chose purple text on a lime background.

author: Glen Buffer
subject: Why did a small photo turn into a giant email?
body:
attached a camera photo and everyone says it
takes ages to collect. It looked quite small on my screen. Does resizing
the window make the attachment smaller?

author: Mara Packet
subject: Re: Why did a small photo turn into a giant email?
body:
The display size and file size are different. Resize a copy of the
actual picture in an image editor and save at suitable JPEG quality;
check the resulting file size before attaching it. Email encoding can
increase the transmitted size too. Keep the original if you need it.

author: Lance Frames
subject: Re: Why did a small photo turn into a giant email?
body:
Put "small photo" in the subject line. The mail server should respect
your artistic intent. Mine has declined to comment.

author: Glen Buffer
subject: Re: Why did a small photo turn into a giant email?
body:
Saved a genuinely smaller copy in this case. It is now
possible to receive the picture before the subject of the picture has
left university. Thanks for explaining the difference.

author: Owen Bundle
subject: Second modem connected: why is one file still slow?
body:
both modems have their CONNECT lights on,
but the download is erratic. Is two lights enough evidence that I have
doubled the useful speed? I have counted them twice to be sure.

author: Ruth Handshake
subject: Re: Second modem connected: why is one file still slow?
body:
Not by itself. Check that both links joined the same bundle and look at
the actual bytes delivered over time. A link can be connected yet lose
traffic or stop responding. Record the initial rates, test a local file,
and compare one link with two rather than guessing from the lights.

author: Kev Baud
subject: Re: Second modem connected: why is one file still slow?
body:
Add two more LEDs to the case. The graph will become much more
convincing. This is decorative advice, not network engineering.

author: Owen Bundle
subject: Re: Second modem connected: why is one file still slow?
body:
in this case the second member was stalling. One-link tests
were steadier. Logging rates and useful bytes made the comparison much
clearer than staring at the front panel until it felt faster.

author: Fern Filename
subject: I edited my page, but the old heading is still there
body:
uploaded a new index.html, and my browser
still shows yesterday's heading. I have accused the FTP program twice.
What should I check before accusing it a third time?

author: Jo Underconstruction
subject: Re: I edited my page, but the old heading is still there
body:
Check the exact URL and uploaded filename first. Then reload the page
and check the browser cache settings; old browsers may reuse a cached
copy. Compare the page source with your local file. If other people can
see the update, that is a useful clue that the upload succeeded.

author: Pete Cassette
subject: Re: I edited my page, but the old heading is still there
body:
Yesterday's heading has seniority. New headings must complete a
probation period before being displayed.

author: Fern Filename
subject: Re: I edited my page, but the old heading is still there
body:
The file was uploaded correctly. Reloading without the stale
cached copy showed the new heading. I have apologised to FTP and am now
considering a small gift basket for the browser.

author: Nicky Retry
subject: Radio and a download: negotiating custody of the modem
body:
listening experiment: 32 kbit/s radio is fine until I download
something else, then the music pauses. Is the station taking dramatic
breaths, or have I asked the line to do too much?

author: DJ Bitbucket
subject: Re: Radio and a download: negotiating custody of the modem
body:
Try 16 kbit/s first and leave some capacity for the download. Audio and
file transfers share the same connection, and overhead needs room too.
Let the initial player buffer fill. If it keeps stopping even without a
download, compare a lower rate and check the underlying link.

author: Pete Cassette
subject: Re: Radio and a download: negotiating custody of the modem
body:

author: Nicky Retry

body:
in this case, 16 kbit/s was steadier while browsing. A large
download could still crowd it out. Apparently bandwidth cannot be created
by ticking "high quality" with sufficient confidence.

author: Bea IRQ
subject: Found a serial cable. How do I tell what it is?
body:
a cable in the box marked MISC. One end
fits a serial port. The other end also fits a serial port. Does that make
it a null-modem cable, or simply a very optimistic straight cable?

author: Mo Exchange
subject: Re: Found a serial cable. How do I tell what it is?
body:
Connector shape alone is not enough. Find its markings or check the
pin connections against the equipment manuals using a continuity tester
with the cable disconnected. Straight and null-modem wiring serve
different purposes; adapters can add another layer of confusion.

author: Baz Swapmeet
subject: Re: Found a serial cable. How do I tell what it is?
body:
The MISC label is the industry standard for "will become essential
approximately one week after you throw it away".

author: Bea IRQ
subject: Re: Found a serial cable. How do I tell what it is?
body:
in this case it was straight-through, with a null-modem
adapter hiding elsewhere in the same box. I have labelled both. The box
has objected that this is contrary to its founding principles.

author: Ash Jumper
subject: Mouse only travels east. Has it chosen a career?
body:
ball mouse moves horizontally but vertical
movement is unreliable. Is it a driver issue or should I inspect the
mechanism before reinstalling everything in sight?

author: Bea IRQ
subject: Re: Mouse only travels east. Has it chosen a career?
body:
With the machine off, check the removable ball and rollers according
to the mouse's instructions. Built-up lint can stop a roller turning.
Avoid soaking the electronics or forcing small clips. If cleaning does
not help, test another mouse before making software changes.

author: Kev Baud
subject: Re: Mouse only travels east. Has it chosen a career?

columns. Ask human resources about vertical development opportunities.

author: Ash Jumper
subject: Re: Mouse only travels east. Has it chosen a career?
body:
The roller had accumulated enough lint to qualify as a small
mammal. Cleaned gently, and the pointer now moves in both directions.
No driver ceremony was required.

author: Owen Bundle
subject: Old disk has started clicking: what first?
body:
an old hard disk has started making
new clicking noises. The files are backed up only in the sense that I
have been thinking about backing them up. What is the sensible next step?

author: Ruth Handshake
subject: Re: Old disk has started clicking: what first?
body:
New noises do not establish the exact fault, but prioritise recovering
important data rather than benchmarking or defragmenting the disk. Avoid
unnecessary writes. If data is irreplaceable or the drive is failing to
read, stop and consider professional recovery rather than repeated tests.
Do not open the drive or rely on folklore repairs.

author: Pete Cassette
subject: Re: Old disk has started clicking: what first?
body:

the backup should come first. My band can use the printer.

author: Owen Bundle
subject: Re: Old disk has started clicking: what first?
body:
in this case I stopped experimenting and made a recovery
plan. The lesson is that "I will copy it next weekend" is not a storage
format, however widely deployed it may be.

author: Fern Filename
subject: Testing quotes, apostrophes and the mysterious dot
body:
> This is a quoted line.

.dot at the beginning of a line
<This is plain text, not an HTML tag.>

subject: Re: Testing quotes, apostrophes and the mysterious dot
body:

author: Mark Ellis
subject: Netscape 16 bit works, 32 bit refuses to connect
body:
Upgraded the 486 from Windows 3.11 last weekend. Old Navigator connects
through Trumpet, new Navigator says it cannot find anything. Same modem,
same phone number. Is the 32 bit version fussier about phone lines?

author: Denise Carter
subject: Re: Netscape 16 bit works, 32 bit refuses to connect
body:
Start by checking which networking stack each program is using. The
older setup and Win95 Dial-Up Networking are not interchangeable merely
because both show a connection. Try the native DUN connection with the
32 bit browser. Note your existing setup before changing it.

author: Pete Cassette
subject: Re: Netscape 16 bit works, 32 bit refuses to connect
body:
This is why I upgrade one application every six months. Gives me five
months to forget what I did to make the previous one work.

body:
Connected using DUN first and the new browser works. The modem was
innocent. Will sort out the older programs before removing anything.
Thanks Denise. Posting this so the next person finds the answer.

author: Colin R
subject: Old mail utility will not bring up the dialler
body:
Small 16 bit mail utility works once I am online, but unlike the browser
it does not start the Win95 dialler. Is this a server setting?

author: Denise Carter
subject: Re: Old mail utility will not bring up the dialler
body:
Probably look at the application and local autodial behaviour first.
If opening DUN manually makes it work, the server connection itself is
not the missing step. Old applications do not all trigger autodial the
same way. Which version of the utility is it?

author: Glen Buffer

author: Andy North
subject: 28800 feels faster than 33600 -- not a typo
body:
Borrowed a second modem. Higher CONNECT number, worse file transfers.
Tested the same ZIP twice. Anyone seen this or am I timing the cache?

author: Ruth Handshake
subject: Re: 28800 feels faster than 33600 -- not a typo
body:
Save the connection logs for both tests and compare error correction,
retries and the actual file bytes transferred. Also make sure both tests
really fetch the file. A high initial rate does not guarantee a clean
sustained connection; do not blame compression without checking the logs.

author: Kev Baud
subject: Re: 28800 feels faster than 33600 -- not a typo
body:
Perhaps 33600 is the speed at which it promises to deliver the bytes,
and 28800 is the speed at which it actually remembers to do so.

author: Andy North
subject: Re: 28800 feels faster than 33600 -- not a typo
body:
Retested with logs. Different error-control reports, plus the quicker
CONNECT was much less steady. Keeping the reliable setup for now.
The stopwatch did better than the box artwork.

subject: Direct cable connection is not talking to NT RAS
body:
Trying a serial link between the spare Win95 PC and an NT machine.
Cable worked in an older setup. Direct Cable Connection gets nowhere.
Both ports are set to 57600, so what am I overlooking?

author: Mo Exchange
subject: Re: Direct cable connection is not talking to NT RAS
body:
Matching port speeds only addresses one part of it. Check the cable
wiring and whether the services on both ends expect compatible framing
and connection setup. Direct Cable Connection is not a promise that it
will talk to any serial service called RAS.

author: Bea IRQ
subject: Re: Direct cable connection is not talking to NT RAS
body:
Please list the actual server version and cable type. "Same as before"
is not enough to tell us whether the software at the two ends agrees.
Also check flow control; do not just buy another cable at random.

author: Colin R
subject: Re: Direct cable connection is not talking to NT RAS
body:
Fair point. I had treated two different connection methods as synonyms.
Will write down the actual combination and start again. Cable has been
returned to the box marked NOT YET PROVEN GUILTY.

author: Lance Frames
subject: Best viewed with... something other than my browser
body:
Put a visitor counter and a scrolling heading on my page. Looks fine
here. A friend says the heading is missing and the table is wider than
his screen. Must I test every browser anybody ever wrote?

author: Jo Underconstruction
subject: Re: Best viewed with... something other than my browser
body:
You can start by making teh essential content readable without teh
extensions. Test anohter browser and a narrow window. A page that loses
its decoration is one thing; a page that loses its navigation is anohter.

author: Mark Ellis
subject: Re: Best viewed with... something other than my browser
body:
I am less worried about which browser wins than whether I can find the
phone number before the background finishes arriving.

author: Lance Frames
subject: Re: Best viewed with... something other than my browser
body:
Removed the scrolling heading and used ordinary links for navigation.
Counter remains because my mum has visited twice and I want evidence.
The page is now readable in the other browser too.

author: Andy North
subject: Will a new modem INF turn my 28.8 into a 33.6?
body:
Found a newer INF with 33600 in the filename. My modem is sold as 28.8.
Is that an upgrade or just Windows learning a new name for it?

author: Bea IRQ
subject: Re: Will a new modem INF turn my 28.8 into a 33.6?
body:
An INF describes the modem to Windows; it does not by itself replace
the modem firmware or hardware. Check the exact model and the vendor's
upgrade documentation. A similar case and a bigger number in a filename
are not enough to establish compatibility.

author: Baz Swapmeet
subject: Re: Will a new modem INF turn my 28.8 into a 33.6?
body:
I have a label maker if that helps. Can offer 33.6, 56K or "experimental
fibre" depending on how much space is available on the front panel.

author: Andy North
subject: Re: Will a new modem INF turn my 28.8 into a 33.6?
body:
Model number checked. This file is for a different revision. Have left
it alone. The label maker may still be useful for identifying the power
supplies, which are apparently breeding.

author: Fern Filename
subject: How long is too long for a signature?
body:
Trying out a signature with the machine specifications, modem settings,
favourite quotation and a small ASCII dragon. It is sixteen lines.
Too much? The dragon alone accounts for half.

author: Mara Packet
subject: Re: How long is too long for a signature?
body:
A short signature makes threads easier to read, particularly on small
screens. Put the full machine details in posts where they help diagnose
the problem. You do not need your IRQ assignments under a recipe.

author: Kev Baud
subject: Re: How long is too long for a signature?
body:
Keep the dragon. Remove the message. Most of us are here for the dragon
by this stage anyway.

author: Fern Filename
subject: Re: How long is too long for a signature?
body:
Down to three lines. The dragon has moved to the homepage, where it has
room to spread out and frighten the visitor counter.

author: Baz Swapmeet
subject: FS: 486 board, CPU and RAM, $60 ono
body:
486 motherboard with DX2/66 and 8 MB. Came from a working desktop last
month. No case or disk. Can include the printed jumper sheet. Asking $60
ono, would consider a decent external modem in part exchange.

Fictional listing.

author: Ash Jumper
subject: Re: FS: 486 board, CPU and RAM, $60 ono
body:
Does it use standard 72-pin SIMMs? Also, is the battery on a flying
lead or soldered to the board? Would like a photo of that area.

author: Andy North
subject: Re: FS: 486 board, CPU and RAM, $60 ono
body:
Hang on to the jumper sheet. Worth considerably more than a promise
that somebody remembers where the little black things went.

author: Baz Swapmeet
subject: Re: FS: 486 board, CPU and RAM, $60 ono
body:
72-pin slots. Will check the battery arrangement before making claims.
Jumper sheet is in the bag with the board, a rare outbreak of organisation.

author: Mark Ellis
subject: Numbers work, names do not
body:
Can reach a page by its numeric address, but names fail. Reconnecting
sometimes helps. Have I configured the wrong sort of TCP/IP?

author: Denise Carter
subject: Re: Numbers work, names do not
body:
Check which DNS servers the dial-up connection receives and whether
name lookups actually succeed through them. Record the settings before
changing anything. Being able to reach an IP narrows the problem, but
does not mean every other part of the connection is correct.

author: Kev Baud
subject: Re: Numbers work, names do not
body:
Computers only understand numbers. Names were a concession to people
who cannot remember the telephone number of the computer shop.

author: Mark Ellis
subject: Re: Numbers work, names do not
body:
The connection had an old DNS setting carried over from another setup.
Corrected that, reconnected, and names now work. Will label the old notes
rather than leaving them beside the current ones. Cheers.

author: Fern Filename
subject: Download stopped at 98 percent. Must I start again?
body:
Large installer nearly finished, then the connection dropped. There is
a partial file on disk. Is there a way to get just the missing bit, or
does the telephone company get another hour of my life?

author: Mara Packet
subject: Re: Download stopped at 98 percent. Must I start again?
body:
It depends on your downloader and the server. Some support resuming a
partial transfer. Keep the partial file, look for a resume option, and
check the final size or supplied checksum afterwards. A nearly complete
installer is not a complete installer.

author: Glen Buffer
subject: Re: Download stopped at 98 percent. Must I start again?
body:
Ninety-eight percent is where my downloads traditionally become a
family event. Everybody has to stop looking at the telephone.

author: Fern Filename
subject: Re: Download stopped at 98 percent. Must I start again?
body:
The download manager resumed it. Checked the completed file rather than
trying to run the fragment. Keeping the manager; retiring the ritual of
promising not to touch anything until the progress bar finishes.

author: Colin R
subject: My replies appear before the messages I am answering
body:
Newsreader has put my latest reply above yesterday's question. Have I
discovered a faster connection, or is the date on this PC important?

author: Mara Packet
subject: Re: My replies appear before the messages I am answering
body:
Check the local date, time and time zone, and whether the clock stays
correct after power off. Readers may sort by date, while threading uses
message relationships. A wrong clock can make a perfectly ordinary
conversation look like correspondence from the future.

author: Nicky Retry
subject: Re: My replies appear before the messages I am answering
body:
If you really can answer before the question, please post tomorrow's
modem lottery results. Failing that, the weather will do.

author: Colin R
subject: Re: My replies appear before the messages I am answering
body:
Clock was a month out. Corrected it and made a note to check it after
shutdown. My career as a time traveller was brief but administratively
complicated.

author: Jo Underconstruction
subject: Text file has odd line breaks after FTP
body:
Uploaded a text file and the line breaks look different on the other
machine. Which transfer mode should I use? I usually click the option
that sounds most modern.

author: Denise Carter
subject: Re: Text file has odd line breaks after FTP
body:
For images, ZIPs and executables, use binary transfer so the bytes are
preserved. Text-mode transfer can change line endings. For a text file,
choose based on what the destination expects; if in doubt, keep an
original and compare a small test file first.

author: Lance Frames
subject: Re: Text file has odd line breaks after FTP
body:
My client says AUTO, which I interpret as "someone else has agreed to
be responsible". So far no one has answered my letters.

author: Jo Underconstruction
subject: Re: Text file has odd line breaks after FTP

author: Tessa Inbox
subject: Two PCs, one mailbox, twice the confusion
body:
Read mail on the desktop, then the laptop says the inbox is empty.
Would like both to see it. Is the second machine connecting too slowly?

author: Mara Packet
subject: Re: Two PCs, one mailbox, twice the confusion
body:
Check whether the first client removes messages from the server after
fetching them. If you choose to leave copies, understand how and when
they will eventually be removed, or the mailbox can accumulate old mail.
Back up important messages before experimenting with client settings.

author: Mark Ellis
subject: Re: Two PCs, one mailbox, twice the confusion
body:
I tried solving this by forwarding everything to myself. Can confirm
that it did not produce a simpler diagram.

author: Tessa Inbox
subject: Re: Two PCs, one mailbox, twice the confusion
body:
The desktop was removing messages. Changed the retention behaviour and
tested with an unimportant message. Both machines now collect it. Will
keep a proper local archive rather than use the server as a cupboard.

author: Nicky Retry
subject: Account page signs me out when I return later
body:
Can sign in, read the account page, then return much later and have to
sign in again. Browser accepts cookies. Is this a fault?

author: Denise Carter
subject: Re: Account page signs me out when I return later
body:
Not necessarily. Sessions can expire, and a service restart can also
end them. Use a fresh sign-in form and check whether it works normally
straight afterwards. Do not post your password or session cookie here.
If it fails immediately, the exact error text would help.

author: Kev Baud
subject: Re: Account page signs me out when I return later
body:
The website has concluded that you have gone outside. A serious breach
of the subscriber agreement, at least in this weather.

author: Nicky Retry
subject: Re: Account page signs me out when I return later
body:
It works immediately; I was coming back after a long break. Will stop
keeping the sign-in form open all afternoon as though it were a reserved
seat. Nothing else appears broken.

author: Fern Filename
subject: GIF or JPEG for the homepage?
body:
One photo, one little logo. Is it worth converting everything to GIF
so the page has only one kind of picture?

author: Jo Underconstruction
subject: Re: GIF or JPEG for teh homepage?
body:
Try JPEG for teh photo and GIF for teh small flat-colour artwork.
Compare actual file sizes and appearance instead of converting merely
for consistency. Keep originals, and do not repeatedly resave teh only
copy while trying quality settings.

author: Pete Cassette
subject: Re: GIF or JPEG for the homepage?
body:
My logo has so few colours that the printer offered to colour it in
by hand. Still larger than the entire text of the page, somehow.

author: Fern Filename
subject: Re: GIF or JPEG for the homepage?
body:
The photo is much smaller as JPEG. The logo looks cleaner as GIF.
Removed an enormous unused border too. It is embarrassing how much
bandwidth I was spending on a rectangle of nothing.

author: Lance Frames
subject: Guestbook etiquette: signing your own guestbook
body:
If I install a guestbook and nobody signs it, may I leave the first
entry myself? Otherwise it looks as though the site opened during a
power cut.

author: Mara Packet
subject: Re: Guestbook etiquette: signing your own guestbook
body:
A welcome entry from the site owner is perfectly understandable. Do
not invent independent endorsements. A short introduction and clear
contact link can be more useful than a guestbook anyway.

author: Kev Baud
subject: Re: Guestbook etiquette: signing your own guestbook
body:
I sign mine "the management". There is only one of me, but we like to
maintain standards.

author: Lance Frames
subject: Re: Guestbook etiquette: signing your own guestbook
body:
Have added a welcome instead of pretending to be my own delighted
visitor. The management wishes to thank the management for implementing
this policy so promptly.

author: Andy North
subject: Somebody already has my IRC nickname
body:
Tried joining IRC with the usual nickname and the server says it is
in use. Is it my old browser connection still sitting there?

author: Mo Exchange
subject: Re: Somebody already has my IRC nickname
body:
Could be an existing connection, or somebody else using the same name.
Try another nickname first. If your previous connection ended abruptly,
allow time for it to disappear. A familiar nickname is not proof that
the person behind it is the same person.

author: Baz Swapmeet
subject: Re: Somebody already has my IRC nickname
body:
I use a nickname nobody else would want. Unfortunately it is now my
nickname and teh strategy has become a personal problem.

author: Andy North
subject: Re: Somebody already has my IRC nickname
body:
Old connection vanished and I got the name back. Have picked a spare
for next time. Thanks for the reminder about names; will not treat a
nickname as a password or an identity check.

author: Mark Ellis
subject: Bookmark takes me to the wrong part of a framed site
body:
Bookmarked a useful page, returned later and got the front page instead.
The site has frames. Did the bookmark forget where I had been?

author: Jo Underconstruction
subject: Re: Bookmark takes me to the wrong part of a framed site
body:
You may have bookmarked the outer frameset rather than the document
shown inside it. Look for a direct link to the actual page, or use your
browser's options for opening that frame separately. Authors can help
by providing ordinary links as well as framed navigation.

author: Lance Frames
subject: Re: Bookmark takes me to the wrong part of a framed site
body:
Frames are useful because they let four separate documents disagree
about which one is the actual page.

author: Mark Ellis
subject: Re: Bookmark takes me to the wrong part of a framed site
body:
Found the direct document URL and that bookmark works. Sent the author
a polite note asking for a direct link. Did not include my first draft,
which was mainly punctuation.

author: Bea IRQ
subject: COM port opens in terminal but not in dial-up
body:
Terminal talks to the modem. Dial-Up Networking says it cannot open
the port. Terminal is still running because I wanted to watch the lights.
Have I found a driver conflict?

author: Ruth Handshake
subject: Re: COM port opens in terminal but not in dial-up
body:
Close the terminal and any other program that may have the port open,
then try DUN again. Test one application at a time before changing IRQs
or drivers. If it still fails, note the exact port and error message.

author: Kev Baud
subject: Re: COM port opens in terminal but not in dial-up
body:
Only one person may hold the steering wheel at a time.
The modem has regrettably rejected our proposal for a committee.

author: Bea IRQ
subject: Re: COM port opens in terminal but not in dial-up
body:
Closing the terminal fixed it. I had left it connected to the port
while asking another application to use that same port. No hardware
changes needed. Leaving this here as a warning to my future self.

author: Ash Jumper
subject: CD-ROM plays audio CDs but not this data disc
body:
Drive will play a music CD, but one data disc refuses to read. Before
I buy a new drive, what is the sensible comparison?

author: Bea IRQ
subject: Re: CD-ROM plays audio CDs but not this data disc
body:
Try a known-good pressed data disc and test the suspect disc in a
second drive. Audio playback alone does not establish that every data
reading path works. Inspect the disc without abrasive experiments and
record whether the failure affects one disc or all data discs.

author: Colin R
subject: Re: CD-ROM plays audio CDs but not this data disc
body:
Please identify the disc type too. "It is silver" has so far failed
to narrow down most of the collection.

author: Ash Jumper
subject: Re: CD-ROM plays audio CDs but not this data disc
body:
Pressed discs work. The troublesome one also fails elsewhere. Will
replace that disc rather than the drive. Saved myself a shopping trip
and acquired a circular object for the box of unresolved questions.

author: Owen Bundle
subject: BIOS sees the new memory, Windows feels much the same
body:
Added RAM. BIOS counts it correctly, but a web page still takes ages
to arrive. Was expecting a more dramatic result for the screwdriver work.

author: Denise Carter
subject: Re: BIOS sees the new memory, Windows feels much the same
body:
More memory helps when the machine was short of it; it does not raise
the modem's line rate. Compare local application switching and disk
activity separately from time spent waiting for network transfers.
Keep the test workload similar before judging the upgrade.

author: Pete Cassette
subject: Re: BIOS sees the new memory, Windows feels much the same
body:
The extra memory is occupied by the expectation that the upgrade will
make everything faster. Very demanding application, that one.

author: Owen Bundle
subject: Re: BIOS sees the new memory, Windows feels much the same
body:
Switching between programs is better and there is less disk thrashing.
The download still arrives at modem speed, as it apparently has every
right to do. Calling the upgrade a success with revised expectations.

author: Lance Frames
subject: 800x600 is readable, 1024x768 is impressive
body:
Can make the old monitor show 1024x768, but the text is tiny. Is the
correct approach to sit nearer, change fonts, or stop showing off?

author: Jo Underconstruction
subject: Re: 800x600 is readable, 1024x768 is impressive
body:
Choose a mode the monitor supports comfortably and which you can
actually read. Check its specifications before changing refresh rates.
Use suitable font settings rather than making every site use enormous
fixed-size text. More pixels are not automatically more usable.

author: Andy North
subject: Re: 800x600 is readable, 1024x768 is impressive
body:
Stop showing off. Keep a screenshot of the larger desktop to prove
that it happened, then return to being able to read the clock.

author: Lance Frames
subject: Re: 800x600 is readable, 1024x768 is impressive
body:
Back to a comfortable supported mode. Can now read error messages
without leaning over the keyboard, which has improved both diagnosis
and the condition of my nose.

author: Baz Swapmeet
subject: FS: flatbed scanner and a frightening amount of software
body:
Flatbed scanner with interface card and driver disks. $40 ono. Was
working before the last desk rearrangement; will test again before any
agreement. Manual included, in a folder marked something unrelated.

Fictional listing.

author: Fern Filename
subject: Re: FS: flatbed scanner and a frightening amount of software
body:
Which interface and exact model? Also need to know whether the driver
disks match the machine I would use, not just whether the scanner lights
up attractively.

author: Bea IRQ
subject: Re: FS: flatbed scanner and a frightening amount of software
body:
Please keep the interface card with it. "Industry standard connector"
on the box is not always the happy ending one hopes for.

author: Baz Swapmeet
subject: Re: FS: flatbed scanner and a frightening amount of software
body:
Will add the model and card details after checking the labels. Keeping
the whole lot together. The folder has been renamed SCANNER, an action
which may invalidate its natural camouflage.

author: Colin R
subject: WTB: small IDE drive for a 486 restoration
body:
Looking for a small IDE hard disk for a 486. Quiet and tested preferred.
Do not need huge capacity; mostly after something the BIOS understands.
Will check the board details before agreeing on a model.

Fictional listing.

author: Ash Jumper
subject: Re: WTB: small IDE drive for a 486 restoration
body:
Have one in a parts box but will identify and test it before offering
it. Please send the board model first; I would rather spend five minutes
checking than have it make a round trip for nothing.

author: Kev Baud
subject: Re: WTB: small IDE drive for a 486 restoration
body:
I have one that is exceptionally quiet when unplugged. Cannot yet
claim this as a meaningful performance advantage.

author: Colin R
subject: Re: WTB: small IDE drive for a 486 restoration
body:
Board details sent. No rush; testing first is appreciated. Restoration
has already waited twenty years and can probably manage another evening.

author: Nicky Retry
subject: Testing thread view after changing newsreaders
body:
Changed newsreaders and this is my first post from the new one. Does
the subject look normal? It offered to add formatting and I told it no.

author: Mara Packet
subject: Re: Testing thread view after changing newsreaders
body:
Subject and plain text look fine. Replying in the same thread so you
can check whether it appears underneath the original message.

author: Glen Buffer
subject: Re: Testing thread view after changing newsreaders
body:
Also visible in the web viewer. No unusual colours, which is a shame
because I was hoping to blame the monitor again.

author: Nicky Retry
subject: Re: Testing thread view after changing newsreaders
body:
Replies are grouped correctly. Have found the setting that stops it
quoting the entire signature as well. Will return to lurking now that
the new software has passed its entrance examination.

author: Doreen Mills
subject: URGENT: cup holder retracts whenever I start Encarta
body:
The motorised cup holder on the new computer is faulty. Every time the
children start Encarta it withdraws my tea into the machine. I have asked
them not to press anything educational while I am drinking.

It says COMPACT DISC on the front. Is that the brand of cup holder?
The shop denies ever supplying a cup holder, which is frankly dishonest.

author: Mo Exchange
subject: Re: URGENT: cup holder retracts whenever I start Encarta
body:
That is the CD-ROM tray. It holds a disc, not a drink. Please keep the
tea away from it. The program is trying to use the drive.

author: Trevor Pike
subject: Re: URGENT: cup holder retracts whenever I start Encarta
body:
Then why is there a perfectly cup-shaped depression? They cannot put
furniture on a computer and retrospectively declare it educational.

author: Doreen Mills
subject: Re: URGENT: cup holder retracts whenever I start Encarta
body:
I have moved the tea to the desk under protest. Encarta now works, but
we have lost a feature. Will the shop refund the difference between a
computer with a cup holder and one without?

author: Stan Rook
subject: Can a ZIP file explode if it is compressed too much?
body:
Downloaded a ZIP which expands from 2 MB to 11 MB. That is a lot of
pressure in a small space. The computer is under the stairs and I would
like to know which direction it will go if the file bursts.

My brother says all the pressure comes out when you unzip it. He has
never been wrong about a bicycle tyre.

author: Ruth Handshake
subject: Re: Can a ZIP file explode if it is compressed too much?
body:
It is a way of representing data using fewer bytes. There is no
physical pressure in the file. Expanding it needs disk space, not a
reinforced cupboard.

author: Trevor Pike
subject: Re: Can a ZIP file explode if it is compressed too much?
body:
The real issue is whether the expanded Internet will fit up the stairs.
Measure the landing before opening any more files.

author: Stan Rook
subject: Re: Can a ZIP file explode if it is compressed too much?
body:
Have cleared disk space, although I do not like that the program calls
it EXTRACT. We are going to do it after the dog has left the hallway.
If the cupboard survives I will mark this solved.

author: Helen Crate
subject: Where is the fire supposed to come out?
body:
A magazine says every computer needs a firewall. We have carpet and
no chimney in the spare room. Does the modem exhaust count, or must we
have a builder in before using the Internet again?

The husband says it is just software. He also said the printer would
pay for itself and it has not earned a cent.

author: Denise Carter
subject: Re: Where is the fire supposed to come out?
body:
A firewall filters network traffic. It is not a heater and installing
one does not create a fire. You do not need to modify the room.

author: Stan Rook
subject: Re: Where is the fire supposed to come out?
body:
Do not let a builder quote by the packet. My cousin did and now his
router has a conservatory.

author: Helen Crate
subject: Re: Where is the fire supposed to come out?
body:
We are keeping the carpet, then. I still want an explanation for the
word BURN on the CD software. This industry needs one person in charge
of naming things who has actually been inside a house.

author: June Ledger
subject: Cookies keep appearing. We do not keep food upstairs.
body:
Found cookies in the browser. Nobody admits bringing them in. I have
asked the children and they say websites leave them, which sounds like
blaming crumbs on the television.

Can they attract ants through the telephone cable? I have already put
the biscuit tin in the other room as a precaution.

author: Mara Packet
subject: Re: Cookies keep appearing. We do not keep food upstairs.
body:
Browser cookies are small pieces of stored data, not food. They can
remember things such as a session. No ants are involved.

author: Doreen Mills
subject: Re: Cookies keep appearing. We do not keep food upstairs.
body:
It is still rude to leave cookies without asking whether anybody would
like one. The entire Internet has forgotten its manners.

author: June Ledger
subject: Re: Cookies keep appearing. We do not keep food upstairs.
body:
Read the settings and now understand enough to stop searching the
keyboard. I remain opposed to websites remembering me when I cannot
remember why I went upstairs. That seems an unfair arrangement.

author: Dale Mercer
subject: Has anybody actually collected their Recycle Bin?
body:
The Windows Recycle Bin is full and the council came yesterday without
taking it. I printed the icon and left it by the gate. They took the
cardboard but not the files.

Do I need a separate collection for spreadsheets? There is nothing about
Lotus in the leaflet.

author: Jo Underconstruction
subject: Re: Has anybody actually collected thier Recycle Bin?
body:
It is a folder on teh computor. You manage it through Windows; teh
council does not collect it. Check what is in it before emptying it.

author: Trevor Pike
subject: Re: Has anybody actually collected their Recycle Bin?
body:
Spreadsheets go out on alternate Thursdays, formulas facing upwards.
No business waste. They are very strict about pivot tables.

author: Dale Mercer
subject: Re: Has anybody actually collected their Recycle Bin?
body:
I restored the family letter before doing anything else. The council
has returned my printed icon with HOUSEHOLD ONLY written on it.
I am no closer to understanding who is in charge of this machine.

author: Helen Crate
subject: Screen saver failed to save anything. Warranty claim?
body:
Left the flying toasters running all afternoon. Power went off and my
letter was gone. What precisely was being saved? We did not even get
any toast.

I paid for a computer, not a collection of little aeroplanes shaped like
kitchen appliances.

author: Bea IRQ
subject: Re: Screen saver failed to save anything. Warranty claim?
body:
The screen saver is not a document backup. Save the letter in the
application while working. The animation does not write your work to
a file.

author: Kev Baud
subject: Re: Screen saver failed to save anything. Warranty claim?
body:
It saved the toasters. There were hundreds before the outage and there
are hundreds now. The conservation programme is a qualified success.

author: Helen Crate
subject: Re: Screen saver failed to save anything. Warranty claim?
body:
Have found Save. It is a little picture of an object nobody here owns.
Meanwhile the actual screen saver contains recognisable household items.
You can see how this misunderstanding occurred.

author: Doreen Mills
subject: 33600 is far too fast for a residential street
body:
Teh modem says it is connected at 33600. Teh limit outside is fifty.
I have asked it to slow down but it only whistles. Are we responsible
if teh information hits somebody's fence?

Please answer before my husband phones teh council again.

author: Ruth Handshake
subject: Re: 33600 is far too fast for a residential street
body:
That number is a data rate in bits per second. It is not teh speed of
a vehicle, and nothign is driving along teh street at that number.

author: Trevor Pike
subject: Re: 33600 is far too fast for a residential street
body:
Ask whether teh council will accept a screenshot as evidence. Teh
information superhighway has been getting away with this for years.

author: Doreen Mills
subject: Re: 33600 is far too fast for a residential street
body:
Council says it is not thier department. Have written 50 on a piece
of paper and put it beside teh modem anyway. Even if it is only a data
rate, it should know teh rules of teh neighbourhood.

author: Dale Mercer
subject: Will the Internet leak out when I disconnect?
body:
Downloaded three pages and would like to keep them overnight. If I
unplug the phone cable, do they stay in the computer or fall out of the
socket? The socket points down.

I have a small bag ready but do not know how much three pages weighs.

author: Mo Exchange
subject: Re: Will the Internet leak out when I disconnect?

author: June Ledger
subject: Re: Will the Internet leak out when I disconnect?
body:
Put the computer upright. Ours is on its side and every recipe now
starts with the ingredients from the next page.

author: Dale Mercer
subject: Re: Will the Internet leak out when I disconnect?
body:
Saved a copy and checked it offline. Still there this morning. The bag
has been returned to the kitchen. Next question: why did the saved page
bring a whole folder of pictures? We only invited the one page.

author: Stan Rook
subject: Laser printer pointed at neighbour. Is this diplomatic?
body:
Bought a laser printer. The paper comes out towards the neighbour's
house. We have had disagreements over the hedge and I do not want this
interpreted as an escalation.

Can I change the direction of the laser in Control Panel? The manual
shows arrows but no range figures.

author: Bea IRQ
subject: Re: Laser printer pointed at neighbour. Is this diplomatic?
body:
Teh laser operates inside teh printer. It is not firing across teh
room or at your neighbour. Use teh printer as assembled and follow the
manual; do not open the internal laser assembly.

author: Trevor Pike
subject: Re: Laser printer pointed at neighbour. Is this diplomatic?
body:
Print a white flag first. Then a polite border agreement about the
paper tray. Avoid sending anything in landscape until talks conclude.

author: Stan Rook
subject: Re: Laser printer pointed at neighbour. Is this diplomatic?
body:
Neighbour came over. He has the same printer and is primarily annoyed
that mine came with a cable. Relations have improved through our shared
opinion of the shop.

author: June Ledger
subject: Email says it is attached. I did not encourage it.
body:
Sent a letter and now there is an attachment. I do not want a personal
relationship with an email. Is this because I ended the message with
"kind regards"?

Would "yours faithfully" make it worse?

author: Mara Packet
subject: Re: Email says it is attached. I did not encourage it.
body:
An attachment is a file included with the message. Check the compose
window for what was added and remove it if you did not intend to send
that file. The closing phrase does not create attachments.

author: Kev Baud
subject: Re: Email says it is attached. I did not encourage it.
body:
Mine is emotionally unavailable. Every reply is an out-of-office
notice. We are giving each other some disk space.

author: June Ledger
subject: Re: Email says it is attached. I did not encourage it.
body:
It was the photograph I added, so that explains it. Have kept the photo
and the kind regards. I would like to apologise to the recipient for the
second email announcing that I needed boundaries.

author: Helen Crate
subject: Hard drive is spinning. Should we expect lift-off?
body:
The salesman says the disk spins thousands of times a minute. This
seems excessive for keeping a few letters. The computer is upstairs.
Are the screws in the desk rated for this?

I have refused to let anyone install Flight Simulator until we know.

author: Ruth Handshake
subject: Re: Hard drive is spinning. Should we expect lift-off?
body:
The disk's platters rotate inside the drive; this is normal operation.
The computer is not trying to fly. The case and drive should stay closed.
If you hear a new unusual noise, describe it rather than opening it.

author: Dale Mercer
subject: Re: Hard drive is spinning. Should we expect lift-off?
body:
Can confirm that installing a flight simulator does not improve the
computer's aerodynamics. We still cannot get it past the landing.

author: Helen Crate
subject: Re: Hard drive is spinning. Should we expect lift-off?
body:
It is making the same ordinary sound it always made. I was alarmed by
the brochure, which describes nearly every component as either screaming
or blistering. Have put the brochure in the recycling instead.

author: Doreen Mills
subject: Who is responsible for putting the Internet away?
body:
The children leave windows open, the history is everywhere and there
are bookmarks in things nobody is reading. When I ask them to tidy the
Internet they say nobody owns it.

Well somebody owns the carpet and would like a little cooperation.

author: Jo Underconstruction
subject: Re: Who is responsible for putting the Internet away?
body:
You can organise your own bookmarks and downloaded files. That does
not reorganise the websites themselves. It may help to agree a few
household folders instead of putting everything on the desktop.

author: Trevor Pike
subject: Re: Who is responsible for putting the Internet away?
body:
I alphabetised mine. Unfortunately Yahoo is now at teh back, so teh
entire search process takes longer.

author: Doreen Mills
subject: Re: Who is responsible for putting the Internet away?
body:
We now have folders for school, letters and things which nobody will
admit downloading. The last one is by far the largest. I have named it
Department of Denials and await the first appeal.

author: zer0_c00l
subject: posting from a T3. try to keep up.
body:
sup dialup peasants.

currently posting over a T3. by the time your modem has finished its
little robot argument i have downloaded the page, read it, disagreed
with it and mirrored it to a second machine out of spite.

-- zer0_c00l
T3 | 128MB RAM | NO WINMODEMS | fear the throughput

author: Mo Exchange
subject: Re: posting from a T3. try to keep up.
body:
Is this your connection, or teh university lab again? Last week you
called teh office printer "my networked PostScript rendering cluster".
It still had teh accounts department's name on it.

author: Doreen Mills
subject: Re: posting from a T3. try to keep up.
body:
Could you use some of this speed to answer the question about my cup
holder? The shop has now referred me to somebody called Optical Storage,
who sounds like he should work for an optician.

author: zer0_c00l
subject: Re: posting from a T3. try to keep up.
body:
ownership is a bourgeois concept. i have physical access and a login.

also the lab closes at nine so if i stop replying it is scheduled
maintenance and absolutely not the caretaker making me leave.

author: xX_CableGod_Xx
subject: CABLE INSTALLED. modem now available as historical exhibit
body:
it is done. cable is IN. no dialling. no screeching. no negotiating with
a relative who wants to telephone somebody for no technical reason.

opened six web pages at once jsut becuase i could. genuinely concerned
that i may finish teh internet before teh weekend.

56k users: please form an orderly queue to witness teh future.

author: Ruth Handshake
subject: Re: CABLE INSTALLED. modem now available as historical exhibit
body:
Glad it works. Please report sustained transfer rates, test duration
and the server used if you want a useful comparison. Opening six cached
pages is not a benchmark, however dramatic the account of it.

author: Kev Baud
subject: Re: CABLE INSTALLED. modem now available as historical exhibit
body:
I opened seven windows on a 486 and heard the hard disk achieve
consciousness. Does that qualify me for cable or an exorcism?

author: xX_CableGod_Xx
subject: Re: CABLE INSTALLED. modem now available as historical exhibit
body:
benchmark currently suspended. installed a browser skin and now teh
computor spends longer drawing teh buttons than fetching teh page.

this is obviously a graphics bottleneck. teh connection remains elite.

author: PacketLord
subject: 7ms ping. seven. milliseconds.
body:
ping is 7ms. SEVEN. i have entered the realm where cause and effect
must submit a support ticket before proceeding.

if your ping has three digits you are not online, you are corresponding.
please do not reply until your packets have had a decent rest.

author: Bea IRQ
subject: Re: 7ms ping. seven. milliseconds.
body:
Seven milliseconds to what? Your gateway, a local machine or the game
server? A number without a destination is mostly decoration. Also,
latency and file-transfer capacity are different measurements.

author: r00tbeer
subject: Re: 7ms ping. seven. milliseconds.
body:
mine is under 1ms to localhost. therefore my network is approximately
seven times more l33t. currently researching a negative-length cable.

author: PacketLord
subject: Re: 7ms ping. seven. milliseconds.
body:
it was the first router. game server is less cooperative.

withdrawing the causal supremacy claim pending negotiations with the
international telephone system. signature will remain unchanged.

author: Mara Packet
subject: re: your 900KB screenshot proving that you have cable
body:
Please stop attaching a full-screen bitmap to every explanation of how
fast your connection is. Some of us can read a transfer rate without a
photograph of the entire desktop.

You have included the taskbar, your wallpaper and a second window which
appears to contain a smaller version of the same screenshot.

author: xX_CableGod_Xx
subject: Re: re: your 900KB screenshot proving that you have cable
body:
the wallpaper is part of the benchmark environment. removing it would
invalidate the conditions under which the result was obtained.

also the bitmap arrives instantly here. cannot reproduce your issue.

author: Doreen Mills
subject: Re: re: your 900KB screenshot proving that you have cable
body:
I waited several minutes for teh picture and all it proves is that you
have a blue background. My computor also has blue. Sometimes nothign
but blue. I do not make people download evidence of it.

author: Mara Packet
subject: Re: re: your 900KB screenshot proving that you have cable
body:
Trim the picture or post the number as text. The point of having a
faster connection is not to make everybody else's connection slower.
Consider this a request to optimise the witness statements.

author: r00tbeer
subject: FTP transfer too fast to read. UI bug?
body:
on cable now. small downloads finish before i can admire the rate.
need a way to slow down the progress window WITHOUT slowing the network.

before anybody suggests a modem: i am asking a technical question, not
requesting a lifestyle downgrade.

author: Denise Carter
subject: Re: FTP transfer too fast to read. UI bug?
body:
Use a larger suitable test file and a timer, or read the completed
transfer statistics. Do not keep downloading the same file just to make
the counter look impressive. Check whether a cache affects the result.

author: zer0_c00l
subject: Re: FTP transfer too fast to read. UI bug?
body:
on the T3 i have this problem with entire operating systems.

not authorised to install them on the lab machines, admittedly, but
that is a political restriction rather than a bandwidth limitation.

author: r00tbeer
subject: Re: FTP transfer too fast to read. UI bug?
body:
found completed-transfer statistics. devastating development: now i
must read numbers instead of watching the little bars.

still faster than you. have not established who "you" is. broadly you.

author: PacketLord
subject: WTB: domestic T3, must work with existing telephone extension
body:
planning T3 to the bedroom. requirements:
- no recurring bill that my father will notice
- existing telephone extension preferred
- should fit through the hole already drilled for the modem lead
- ideally supplier accepts a sound card in part exchange

please, serious technical answers only. i know what i am doing.

author: Mo Exchange
subject: Re: WTB: domestic T3, must work with existing telephone extension
body:
That is a leased telecom service, not a modem upgrade you plug into
the existing phone extension. Get an actual availability and cost quote
before planning the hole. I suspect the bill condition ends the project.

author: Stan Rook
subject: Re: WTB: domestic T3, must work with existing telephone extension
body:
Will this make teh compressed files more dangerous? I have only jsut
reassured teh family abotu the pressure in the ZIPs. If this line can
put forty Internet files into the cupboard simultaneously we need notice.

author: PacketLord
subject: Re: WTB: domestic T3, must work with existing telephone extension
body:
project temporarily reclassified as "using the college connection".

father has offered domestic access to the lawn mower. zero latency,
dedicated capacity, compulsory weekend service window. negotiations
remain hostile.

author: Andy North
subject: Quake freezes every time somebody wants a cup of tea
body:
Saturday night Quake is fine until somebody in the house decides to
telephone a relative. Then my opponent teleports, I become a stain and
the modem hangs up. They say "it will only take a minute" as though the
other team has agreed to stop shooting during family administration.

author: Ruth Handshake
subject: Re: Quake freezes every time somebody wants a cup of tea
body:
If the call interrupts the same phone line, the game cannot keep the
connection alive by force of will. Agree on a time to use the line.
If you are also seeing trouble without calls, keep those tests separate.

author: Doreen Mills
subject: Re: Quake freezes every time somebody wants a cup of tea
body:
The relative was checking whether we wanted a spare kettle. Some of us
are conducting useful business rather than arguing inside a brown castle.

author: Andy North
subject: Re: Quake freezes every time somebody wants a cup of tea
body:
I offered to telephone about the kettle after the match. Was informed
that the kettle might be gone by then. Apparently the used-appliance
market has lower latency requirements than competitive Quake.

author: r00tbeer
subject: 999 ping. I am watching my own death on a delay.
body:
joined a Quake server and got 999. i fired a rocket, made a sandwich,
and returned in time to discover it had killed the person i used to be.

is the server particularly far away or is my modem sending the packets
individually with a covering letter?

author: Mo Exchange
subject: Re: 999 ping. I am watching my own death on a delay.
body:
What server, which connection and what else was transferring? Try a
nearer server with downloads stopped, and compare at another time.
A high game ping alone does not identify which part of the path is bad.

author: Kev Baud
subject: Re: 999 ping. I am watching my own death on a delay.
body:
Please include sandwich type. If it was toasted, this is considerably
more serious than a basic cheese event.

author: r00tbeer
subject: Re: 999 ping. I am watching my own death on a delay.
body:
nearby server much better. also discovered the browser was fetching a
large picture of a graphics card. apparently my pursuit of performance
was consuming the performance. sandwich was ordinary cheese.

author: Ash Jumper
subject: Doom still judders. Friend says cable would fix my 486.
body:
Doom is choppy even when I am playing on my own. A mate says getting
cable will sort out the ping. I am not actually connected to anything.
Is this an especially bad case of lag?

author: Bea IRQ
subject: Re: Doom still judders. Friend says cable would fix my 486.
body:
If it happens in a local single-player game, start with the machine,
settings and workload. A faster Internet connection will not make local
rendering faster. Separate frame rate from network delay before spending
money on either a modem or a graphics upgrade.

author: xX_CableGod_Xx
subject: Re: Doom still judders. Friend says cable would fix my 486.
body:
cable improves morale, though. since installation i have blamed all
remaining problems on the processor with unprecedented confidence.

author: Ash Jumper
subject: Re: Doom still judders. Friend says cable would fix my 486.
body:
Reduced the display workload and it is smoother. Will save the cable
proposal for something it might actually improve. Friend now says the
real problem is the chair, so his diagnostic privileges are suspended.

author: PacketLord
subject: Ping compensation should include my score
body:
lost 18 to 2. opponent had lower ping. therefore my correct score is
at least 18, perhaps 24 if we account for international routing.

requesting a recognised formula that converts latency into the frags i
would obviously have achieved under laboratory conditions.

author: Mara Packet
subject: Re: Ping compensation should include my score
body:
A connection disadvantage is real, but it does not tell you which shots
you would have landed. You could compare on teh same server and record
teh conditions. Awarding yourself kills is less reproducible.

author: Trevor Pike
subject: Re: Ping compensation should include my score
body:
We apply the same system to bowls. If it rains I am retrospectively
champion of the district. The club has refused to update the board.

author: PacketLord
subject: Re: Ping compensation should include my score
body:
reviewed the match. one death involved walking backwards into lava.
this may have been local prediction. the remaining seventeen are still
under independent investigation by me.

author: Dale Mercer
subject: Doom between two PCs: shall I buy two Internet accounts?
body:
Two computers in the same room, wanting to play Doom. Brother suggests
we both dial out so the game can travel to the Internet and come back.
Seems a long journey when the machines are six feet apart.

author: Denise Carter
subject: Re: Doom between two PCs: shall I buy two Internet accounts?
body:
Check what connection methods your exact game versions support. A
compatible local arrangement can avoid sending traffic out and back,
but the right cable, network setup or software depends on the versions.
List those before buying accounts or adapters.

author: zer0_c00l
subject: Re: Doom between two PCs: shall I buy two Internet accounts?
body:
on the T3 we solve this by having more computers than friends. network
configuration is technically flawless. social layer remains offline.

author: Dale Mercer
subject: Re: Doom between two PCs: shall I buy two Internet accounts?
body:
Will identify the versions first. Brother has accepted that distance
across the carpet and distance through the Internet are not equivalent.
He still insists his machine should host because it has a larger case.

author: xX_CableGod_Xx
subject: Who is listening to radio during my match?
body:
temporarily back on dialup. circumstances beyond my control. do NOT
update your address books.

Quake becomes dreadful when the radio is playing. this is unacceptable.
i should not have to choose between being elite and having a soundtrack.

author: DJ Bitbucket
subject: Re: Who is listening to radio during my match?

author: Doreen Mills
subject: Re: Who is listening to radio during my match?
body:
We had a soundtrack before the Internet. It was called the radio and
it did not stop the children from losing at their games. Highly efficient.

author: xX_CableGod_Xx
subject: Re: Who is listening to radio during my match?
body:
physical radio acquired. game improved. had forgotten that receiving
music through the air is a separate networking technology.

please refer to my present connection as legacy compatibility mode.

author: zer0_c00l
subject: My ping is one. Why am I still losing?
body:
LAN game. ping approximately one. mouse freshly cleaned. keyboard
angled for optimum packet flow. lost repeatedly to somebody who calls
the monitor "the television bit".

requesting known faults in the concept of fairness.

author: Bea IRQ
subject: Re: My ping is one. Why am I still losing?
body:
At that point look at the game rather than the connection. Low latency
removes one obstacle; it does not provide map knowledge, timing or aim.
You could ask the other player what they are doing differently.

author: Kev Baud
subject: Re: My ping is one. Why am I still losing?
body:
Have you tried sending your boasts in smaller packets? The present
volume may be exhausting the opponent's capacity to care.

author: zer0_c00l
subject: Re: My ping is one. Why am I still losing?
body:
asked. apparently they know where the armour respawns. i had spent
most of the evening explaining the hub.

will study the map. under protest. networking remains impeccable.

author: Nicky Retry
subject: Server is perfect at 2am. Can everyone else go to bed?
body:
Same server, same modem, miserable after dinner and lovely in the early
hours. Have considered a polite notice asking the entire country to
stop using the telephone network while I am playing Quake.

author: Mo Exchange
subject: Re: Server is perfect at 2am. Can everyone else go to bed?
body:
Keep timed comparisons and note packet loss as well as latency. Load
somewhere on teh path could vary, but a time pattern does not locate teh
bottleneck by itself. Compare anohter server before blaming one machine.

author: Stan Rook
subject: Re: Server is perfect at 2am. Can everyone else go to bed?
body:
Happy to cooperate, but require written assurance that your late-night
rockets will not disturb the compressed files under our stairs.

author: Nicky Retry
subject: Re: Server is perfect at 2am. Can everyone else go to bed?
body:
Tried a second server and it behaves differently. Keeping notes now.
National bedtime proposal remains in draft because I cannot find the
email address for whoever is in charge of everybody.

author: Rachel M
subject: Who keeps putting an empty milk bottle back in the fridge?
body:
Flat meeting tonight. Somebody has developed the ability to leave
exactly one teaspoon of milk in the bottle, thereby technically not
finishing it and avoiding the trip to the dairy.

We have five adults, three rolls of masking tape with names on them and
no milk. Is this normal flatting or an advanced economics experiment?

author: Pete Cassette
subject: Re: Who keeps putting an empty milk bottle back in the fridge?
body:
Our flat tried individual milk. Required more shelf space than teh
fridge possessed. We now have communal milk and individual accusations.

author: Doreen Mills
subject: Re: Who keeps putting an empty milk bottle back in the fridge?
body:
Put a pencil mark beside the level before bed. This is how we tracked
down the person consuming the cooking sherry. Turned out to be the cook,
which complicated disciplinary proceedings.

author: Rachel M
subject: Re: Who keeps putting an empty milk bottle back in the fridge?
body:
Meeting result: we are buying a second bottle and rotating the dairy
run. The person responsible arrived with a carton of juice and has been
appointed secretary because he clearly understands loopholes.

author: Helen Crate
subject: Telecom bill has arrived. Nobody admits knowing Wellington.
body:
There are toll calls to Wellington on the flat phone bill. Everybody
claims to know nobody there. Apparently the capital is populated entirely
by people unrelated to us.

I am not dividing this equally until somebody recognises a number.

author: June Ledger
subject: Re: Telecom bill has arrived. Nobody admits knowing Wellington.
body:
Keep a notebook by teh phone for toll calls and agree how shared costs
are divided. Work out teh existing mystery before creating a second
mystery abotu teh arithmetic.

author: Trevor Pike
subject: Re: Telecom bill has arrived. Nobody admits knowing Wellington.
body:
Ask whether anyone has been ringing a radio competition. A flatmate
once maintained that a chance to win a toaster constituted investment.

author: Helen Crate
subject: Re: Telecom bill has arrived. Nobody admits knowing Wellington.
body:
Found it. Someone was calling about a job and did not think interviews
counted because he was not enjoying the conversation. Notebook installed.
No ruling yet on whether unemployment excuses the stationery costs.

author: Rachel M
subject: Video shop: all new releases out, every action sequel available
body:
Went down after tea to get a video. Everything we agreed on was out.
Spent forty minutes discussing a film neither of us wanted, then hired
somthing becuase it was starting to rain outside.

Surely there is a better system than reading teh backs of boxes until
one person becomes too tired to object?

author: Stan Rook
subject: Re: Video shop: all new releases out, every action sequel available
body:
Choose two titles before leaving home. Then spend forty minutes arguing
about which unwanted third title most closely resembles either of them.
It is a social occasion, not a distribution problem.

author: Mark Ellis
subject: Re: Video shop: all new releases out, every action sequel available
body:
Our flat has a veto rule. Each person may reject one film. Unfortunately
it has taught us that we dislike more films than there are people.

author: Rachel M
subject: Re: Video shop: all new releases out, every action sequel available
body:
Watched teh consolation rental. Best bit was teh trailer. Now trying to
find that film, which teh shop has only on a box that says COMING SOON.
We are trapped inside a promotional cycle.

author: Graham S
subject: So which household are we watching the rugby at now?
body:
Trying to organise the weekend's rugby. Some matches appear to require
knowing somebody with Sky, which has turned my social life into a survey
of other people's television subscriptions.

If we are all going to one flat, who brings the chips and who sits on
the chair with the broken spring?

author: Mo Exchange
subject: Re: So which household are we watching the rugby at now?
body:
Confirm who actually has the match before buying supplies. Last time
we arrived with enough food for a small tour party and watched a replay
of something our host had already told us the result of.

author: Trevor Pike
subject: Re: So which household are we watching the rugby at now?
body:
Broken-spring chair goes to teh person who talks through teh commentary.
It is important that penalties apply consistently at domestic level.

author: Graham S
subject: Re: So which household are we watching the rugby at now?
body:
Venue found. Host says shoes off and no arguments with the television.
Nobody agreed to the second condition, but we all nodded to preserve
access to the lounge.

author: Colin R
subject: Auckland to Wellington: departure time now a constitutional issue
body:
Driving down for teh weekend. I say leave before dawn. Passenger says
nothign sensible happens before breakfast. Anohter wants to stop at
every place selling a large meat pie.

At present we expect to reach Hamilton sometime after an argument.

author: Rachel M
subject: Re: Auckland to Wellington: departure time now a constitutional issue
body:
Agree the first stop before you leave, and take turns driving if both
are rested and able. A schedule that depends on nobody needing a break
will not survive the first thermos.

author: Doreen Mills
subject: Re: Auckland to Wellington: departure time now a constitutional issue
body:
We always stop when the driver gets cross. Sometimes this means buying
a pie before we have left our own suburb, but road safety is important.

author: Colin R
subject: Re: Auckland to Wellington: departure time now a constitutional issue
body:
Leaving early with breakfast packed. Teh pie enthusiast has produced
a list of stops on a folded road map. It looks less like a trip and
more like a regional inspection of pastry standards.

author: June Ledger
subject: Supermarket queue: why is the fastest checkout never mine?
body:
Changed queues twice and watched both abandoned queues move faster.
The person ahead then produced coupons, a question about potatoes and
a cheque book. I had a loaf of bread and hopes for the afternoon.

Is there an accepted method of choosing, or does the building know?

author: Stan Rook
subject: Re: Supermarket queue: why is the fastest checkout never mine?
body:
Stay in teh first queue. It will not be quicker, but it reduces teh
number of seperate mistakes available for your family to discuss.

author: Trevor Pike
subject: Re: Supermarket queue: why is the fastest checkout never mine?
body:
Choose the one behind the man carrying only batteries. He has either
a very simple purchase or an argument about which packet was on special.
There is no middle ground.

author: June Ledger
subject: Re: Supermarket queue: why is the fastest checkout never mine?
body:
Next time I am going to the dairy. It may cost more, but I can finish
the transaction before becoming personally invested in a stranger's
choice of tinned fruit.

author: Rachel M
subject: Flatmate wanted: must understand that the lounge is not a shed
body:
Room in an established flat. Looking for someone who pays their share,
cleans the bathroom occasionally and does not rebuild a motorcycle
between the sofa and the television.

Last requirement has regrettably needed to be stated. Shared phone,
no smoking inside, references appreciated.

Fictional listing.

author: Bea IRQ
subject: Re: Flatmate wanted: must understand that teh lounge is not a shed
body:
Define "rebuild". Is a carburettor on newspaper acceptable if it is
only there overnight? Asking becuase your last flatmate may be applying
under a different spelling of his first name.

author: Kev Baud
subject: Re: Flatmate wanted: must understand that the lounge is not a shed
body:
Does the room have enough sockets for two computers? I can promise no
motorcycles, but the power arrangements may attract the same objections.

author: Rachel M
subject: Re: Flatmate wanted: must understand that the lounge is not a shed
body:
No engine parts in the lounge. No extension leads across the hall.
