Applicant who asked whether visitors may "occasionally" sleep in the
bath has not progressed to the next stage.

author: Doreen Mills
subject: Television remote has disappeared again. Household paralysed.
body:
Nobody can find teh remote. Teh television is showing teh wrong channel
and four perfectly healthy peopel are sitting beside it discussing teh
problem as though we are snowed in.

I have suggested teh buttons on the front. This was not well received.

author: Mark Ellis
subject: Re: Television remote has disappeared again. Household paralysed.
body:
Look under teh Listener, inside teh sofa and beside whoever last said
"I am not watching this". Those are teh usual three storage locations.

author: Graham S
subject: Re: Television remote has disappeared again. Household paralysed.
body:
Our remote lives on top of teh television, which does defeat part of
teh original concept. Still saves walking back after pressing a button,
provided you do not think abotu it too long.

author: Doreen Mills
subject: Re: Television remote has disappeared again. Household paralysed.
body:
Found in teh kitchen beside teh cordless phone. My husband has spent
teh evening trying to turn up teh news with teh telephone. He says teh
buttons are too similar. Teh telephone has significantly more numbers.

author: Dale Mercer
subject: Who borrowed the good chilly bin?
body: Camping gear has returned except teh only chilly bin with a lid. Suspects have been invited to explain.

author: Jo Underconstruction
subject: Re: Who borrowed the good chilly bin?
body: Ask who unpacked teh car. Ours generally travels from boot to somebody else's garage.

author: Trevor Pike
subject: Re: Who borrowed teh good chilly bin?
body: Advertise a barbecue. It will reappear full of somebody else's sausages.

author: Dale Mercer
subject: Re: Who borrowed the good chilly bin?
body: Found it at my brother's. He thought we had upgraded to warm drinks.

author: Tessa Inbox
subject: Flat inspection versus drying washing
body: Landlord coming tomorrow. Rain all week. Lounge looks like a sock exhibition.

author: Bea IRQ
subject: Re: Flat inspection versus drying washing
body: Move nothign against heaters. Better a visible drying rack than damaged clothes or a hazard.

author: Pete Cassette
subject: Re: Flat inspection versus drying washing
body: Describe it as a textile installation and put an admission charge on teh door.

author: Tessa Inbox
subject: Re: Flat inspection versus drying washing
body: Leaving teh rack up. Have cleaned everything except teh weather.

author: Andy North
subject: Bach keys have gone north without us
body: Keys to teh bach are in a cousin's glovebox. Cousin heading in teh opposite direction.

author: Mo Exchange
subject: Re: Bach keys have gone north without us
body: Sort out who has spare keys before everyone sets off.

author: Lance Frames
subject: Re: Bach keys have gone north without us
body: We have a key cupboard at teh bach. Brilliant system once you get inside.

author: Andy North
subject: Re: Bach keys have gone north without us
body: Spare located. Our holiday will now begin with only teh usual arguments.

author: Ash Jumper
subject: Does every garage contain one unexplained fridge?
body: Helping Dad clear teh garage. Three fridges, only one connected. None may apparently be discarded.

author: Mara Packet
subject: Re: Does every garage contain one unexplained fridge?
body: Ask him to demonstrate which one works before you arrange removal.

author: r00tbeer
subject: Re: Does every garage contain one unexplained fridge?
body: A garage fridge is a retirement home for beetroot jars.

author: Ash Jumper
subject: Re: Does every garage contain one unexplained fridge?
body: One workign spare, one cupboard, one apparently an investment. Negotiations ongoing.

author: Stan Rook
subject: School fair white elephant table
body: Donated a lamp. Mum bought it back becuase she recognised teh shade.

author: Denise Carter
subject: Re: School fair white elephant table
body: Put next year's donations somewhere she will not inspect them first.

author: PacketLord
subject: Re: School fair white elephant table
body: Our household economy is entirely based on rebuying teh same fondue set.

author: Stan Rook
subject: Re: School fair white elephant table
body: Lamp back in lounge. School richer; family no wiser.

author: Owen Bundle
subject: Sunday roast versus the last bus
body: Mum insists there is time for pudding. Bus timetable disagrees.

author: Ruth Handshake
subject: Re: Sunday roast versus the last bus
body: Check teh actual departure and leave enough time to get there.

author: Kev Baud
subject: Re: Sunday roast versus teh last bus
body: Mothers use a seperate timetable in which every bus waits for custard.

author: Owen Bundle
subject: Re: Sunday roast versus the last bus
body: Caught it with pudding in a container. Driver declined to judge teh dispute.

author: Fern Filename
subject: Rain on the washing: regional conspiracy?
body: Clear while I was at work. Rain began precisely when teh sheets went outside.

author: Jo Underconstruction
subject: Re: Rain on the washing: regional conspiracy?
body: Check teh forecast before blaming teh neighbour's cloud arrangements.

author: Trevor Pike
subject: Re: Rain on teh washing: regional conspiracy?
body: Bring them inside. Sunshine will immediately return out of spite.

author: Fern Filename
subject: Re: Rain on the washing: regional conspiracy?
body: They are inside. It is now brilliant outside. Theory strengthened.

author: Mark Ellis
subject: Everybody is parking outside our house
body: Nobody owns teh space, apparently. Then why does it feel personally reserved?

author: Bea IRQ
subject: Re: Everybody is parking outside our house
body: Talk to neighbours rather than leaving angry notes under random wipers.

author: Pete Cassette
subject: Re: Everybody is parking outside our house
body: Paint your car to resemble a wheelie bin. They seem to stay wherever they like.

author: Mark Ellis
subject: Re: Everybody is parking outside our house
body: Had a civil conversation. Less satisfying than a note, but considerably more effective.

author: Graham S
subject: Potluck dinner with six potato salads
body: Six households independently selected teh easiest respectable contribution. No main course in sight.

author: Mo Exchange
subject: Re: Potluck dinner with six potato salads
body: Agree who brings which type of dish before shopping.

author: Lance Frames
subject: Re: Potluck dinner with six potato salads
body: At least nobody can complain abotu a shortage of potatoes or mayonnaise.

author: Graham S
subject: Re: Potluck dinner with six potato salads
body: We bought bread. It became a salad appreciation evening.

author: Doreen Mills
subject: Dairy counter queue-jumping standards
body: Person buying a newspaper thinks they outrank my bread and milk. Is there a national ranking?

author: Mara Packet
subject: Re: Dairy counter queue-jumping standards
body: Ask politely if somebody is in a hurry. Nobody needs a constitutional dispute over bread.

author: r00tbeer
subject: Re: Dairy counter queue-jumping standards
body: Scratch tickets automatically add twenty minutes to every queue in the building.

author: Doreen Mills
subject: Re: Dairy counter queue-jumping standards
body: Got home eventually. Milk remained cold; opinion of humanity did not.

author: Colin R
subject: Who controls the flat stereo?
body: One person bought it. Four people must listen. Nobody remembers agreeing to his music.

author: Denise Carter
subject: Re: Who controls the flat stereo?
body: Agree some shared hours and let people use headphones when tastes diverge.

author: PacketLord
subject: Re: Who controls the flat stereo?
body: Turn the balance control fully left. Half the argument disappears.

author: Colin R
subject: Re: Who controls the flat stereo?
body: We now have a roster. It is being ignored with impressive consistency.

author: Nicky Retry
subject: New flatmate owns exactly one plate
body: He washes it immediately, leaving everybody else's dishes untouched. Technically faultless. Deeply irritating.

author: Ruth Handshake
subject: Re: New flatmate owns exactly one plate
body: Agree separately on washing-up duties and ownership of crockery.

author: Kev Baud
subject: Re: New flatmate owns exactly one plate
body: Buy one plate each and eat in the driveway. The flat will become a collection of embassies.

author: Nicky Retry
subject: Re: New flatmate owns exactly one plate
body: We discussed it. He now washes communal pans and remains smug about the plate.

author: Helen Crate
subject: Borrowed the trailer, inherited a wardrobe
body: Went to collect a trailer. Uncle says wardrobe can come too. No room in my house.

author: Jo Underconstruction
subject: Re: Borrowed the trailer, inherited a wardrobe
body: Make clear what you agreed to transport before hitching up.

author: Trevor Pike
subject: Re: Borrowed the trailer, inherited a wardrobe
body: Every borrowed trailer carries a hidden compulsory furniture subscription.

author: Helen Crate
subject: Re: Borrowed the trailer, inherited a wardrobe
body: Returned both. Uncle disappointed, doorway relieved.

author: June Ledger
subject: Holiday photos: six rolls of thumbs
body: Got prints back. Landscapes dominated by a large pink object.

author: Bea IRQ
subject: Re: Holiday photos: six rolls of thumbs
body: Check finger placement and keep a few practice shots for the next roll.

author: Pete Cassette
subject: Re: Holiday photos: six rolls of thumbs
body: At least the family can identify who took them without reading the envelope.

author: June Ledger
subject: Re: Holiday photos: six rolls of thumbs
body: Camera has received instruction. Photographer refuses to accept the pink object was local.

author: Rachel M
subject: Saturday lawns versus sleeping in
body: Neighbour starts mowing early. I retaliate by being profoundly annoyed behind closed curtains.

author: Mo Exchange
subject: Re: Saturday lawns versus sleeping in
body: Try a friendly conversation about times rather than escalating machinery.

author: Lance Frames
subject: Re: Saturday lawns versus sleeping in
body: Offer to mow his lawn at midnight. He will at least understand the abstract concept.

author: Rachel M
subject: Re: Saturday lawns versus sleeping in
body: Spoke to him. Later start agreed. My revenge mower stays .

author: Dale Mercer
subject: Why does the beach bag contain a spanner?
body: Packing for the beach revealed a spanner, three pegs and no sunscreen.

author: Mara Packet
subject: Re: Why does the beach bag contain a spanner?
body: Check the bag before leaving and pack what you actually need.

author: r00tbeer
subject: Re: Why does the beach bag contain a spanner?
body: That is the emergency spanner for tightening the tide.

author: Dale Mercer
subject: Re: Why does the beach bag contain a spanner?
body: Nobody has claimed it. Taking it out feels like tempting a very specific disaster.

author: Tessa Inbox
subject: One thermostat, five opinions
body: Flat temperature decided by whoever most recently walked past the heater.

author: Denise Carter
subject: Re: One thermostat, five opinions
body: Agree safe heater use and a setting, then stop secretly changing it.

author: PacketLord
subject: Re: One thermostat, five opinions
body: Put an unconnected dial beside it. Half the flat only wants to participate.

author: Tessa Inbox
subject: Re: One thermostat, five opinions
body: Agreed a setting. Everyone is now wearing different jumpers and claiming victory.

author: Andy North
subject: Phone message says ring Dave
body: There are three Daves. Message includes neither number nor context.

author: Ruth Handshake
subject: Re: Phone message says ring Dave
body: Ask people to write the number, date and what the caller wanted.

author: Kev Baud
subject: Re: Phone message says ring Dave
body: Ring all three and start every call with 'you know why'.

author: Andy North
subject: Re: Phone message says ring Dave
body: Correct Dave located. He wanted to borrow something we lent to a different Dave.

author: Ash Jumper
subject: Family picnic and the missing can opener
body: Excellent picnic. Tinned fruit sealed against all human intervention.

author: Jo Underconstruction
subject: Re: Family picnic and the missing can opener
body: Check utensils before packing. Do not improvise with unsafe tools.

author: Trevor Pike
subject: Re: Family picnic and the missing can opener
body: Invite somebody known to carry an entire workshop in the boot.

author: Ash Jumper
subject: Re: Family picnic and the missing can opener
body: Fruit came home unopened. We ate the sandwiches in a spirit of defeat.

author: Stan Rook
subject: Is the Listener communal property?
body: Flatmate keeps taking it to work. I pay half and have not seen the crossword.

author: Bea IRQ
subject: Re: Is the Listener communal property?
body: Agree where the shared copy stays or buy separate copies.

author: Pete Cassette
subject: Re: Is the Listener communal property?
body: Photocopy the custody agreement and file it under entertainment.

author: Stan Rook
subject: Re: Is the Listener communal property?
body: It stays in the lounge now. Crossword already completed by the mediator.

author: Owen Bundle
subject: The good towels have a classification system
body: Visitors get towels nobody living here is permitted to use. How does one qualify?

author: Mo Exchange
subject: Re: The good towels have a classification system
body: Ask before taking them. This is a household custom, not an objective towel hierarchy.

author: Lance Frames
subject: Re: The good towels have a classification system
body: Leave and ring the doorbell. You are now a guest.

author: Owen Bundle
subject: Re: The good towels have a classification system
body: Tried asking. Apparently I must bring somebody from out of town.

author: Fern Filename
subject: Tea bags in the sink: a growing collection
body: Flatmate believes the sink is a tea-bag marshalling yard.

author: Mara Packet
subject: Re: Tea bags in the sink: a growing collection
body: Put a small container nearby and agree who empties it.

author: r00tbeer
subject: Re: Tea bags in the sink: a growing collection
body: Once they reach sufficient numbers they will elect a drainage commissioner.

author: Fern Filename
subject: Re: Tea bags in the sink: a growing collection
body: Container supplied. It is now full beside a sink containing more tea bags.

author: Mark Ellis
subject: The neighbour's cat has acquired a flat key
body: Cat gets in without invitation and sleeps on the clean washing.

author: Denise Carter
subject: Re: The neighbour's cat has acquired a flat key
body: Check doors and windows before assuming it has developed locksmith skills.

author: PacketLord
subject: Re: The neighbour's cat has acquired a flat key
body: Charge it a share of the power bill. It will move immediately.

author: Mark Ellis
subject: Re: The neighbour's cat has acquired a flat key
body: Window secured. Cat watching through glass like an unpaid landlord.

author: Graham S
subject: Bus driver knows my stop better than I do
body: Nodded off. Driver woke me at the correct stop. Feeling grateful and slightly predictable.

author: Ruth Handshake
subject: Re: Bus driver knows my stop better than I do
body: Thank the driver. Being a familiar passenger can be useful.

author: Kev Baud
subject: Re: Bus driver knows my stop better than I do
body: Change stops tomorrow to maintain an air of mystery.

author: Graham S
subject: Re: Bus driver knows my stop better than I do
body: Said thanks. He said 'again?' so the mystery option may be overdue.

author: Doreen Mills
subject: BBQ roster has become a management structure
body: Eight people supervising one person turning sausages. Nobody cutting bread.

author: Jo Underconstruction
subject: Re: BBQ roster has become a management structure
body: Give each person an actual task instead of another opinion.

author: Trevor Pike
subject: Re: BBQ roster has become a management structure
body: The person holding the tongs outranks everybody until the last sausage.

author: Doreen Mills
subject: Re: BBQ roster has become a management structure
body: Bread arrived. Committee remains convinced it improved the sausages by observing them.

author: Colin R
subject: Flat wanted: no midnight vacuuming
body: Looking for a room where the vacuum cleaner does not start after midnight.

author: Bea IRQ
subject: Re: Flat wanted: no midnight vacuuming
body: Ask about work hours and household routines before agreeing to move.

author: Pete Cassette
subject: Re: Flat wanted: no midnight vacuuming
body: Ours is quiet after midnight because nobody has found the vacuum since March.

author: Colin R
subject: Re: Flat wanted: no midnight vacuuming
body: Will ask practical questions. Was previously distracted by a room with actual curtains.

author: Nicky Retry
subject: Are all spare keys slightly mysterious?
body: Key tin contains nineteen keys. Four fit current locks. Nobody will throw the others away.

author: Mo Exchange
subject: Re: Are all spare keys slightly mysterious?
body: Label known keys while you still remember them. Keep unknown ones separate.

author: Lance Frames
subject: Re: Are all spare keys slightly mysterious?
body: The unknown keys belong to furniture nobody admits owning.

author: Nicky Retry
subject: Re: Are all spare keys slightly mysterious?
body: Labelled four. Remaining fifteen now in a tin marked INHERITANCE.

author: Helen Crate
subject: Road atlas folded by the opposition
body: Passenger opened the map. Nobody can return it to its original arrangement.

author: Mara Packet
subject: Re: Road atlas folded by the opposition
body: Fold along the existing creases slowly rather than forcing new ones.

author: r00tbeer
subject: Re: Road atlas folded by the opposition
body: The map has expanded to its true scale. Buy a larger car.

author: Helen Crate
subject: Re: Road atlas folded by the opposition
body: Arrived. Map travelling home flat across the back seat like a dignitary.

author: June Ledger
subject: Borrowing a video requires a treaty
body: Friend loaned a tape. His instructions are longer than the film.

author: Denise Carter
subject: Re: Borrowing a video requires a treaty
body: Agree when it is coming back and treat it carefully.

author: PacketLord
subject: Re: Borrowing a video requires a treaty
body: Return a written report on the tracking adjustment to demonstrate respect.

author: June Ledger
subject: Re: Borrowing a video requires a treaty
body: Returned on time. He inspected the case with more care than my landlord inspects the flat.

author: Rachel M
subject: Who finished teh emergency biscuits?
body: Emergency biscuit tin empty. Household unanimously denies an emergency.

author: Ruth Handshake
subject: Re: Who finished teh emergency biscuits?
body: Decide whether emergency biscuits are actually shared snacks with a dramatic name.

author: Kev Baud
subject: Re: Who finished the emergency biscuits?
body: My emergency was seeing that there were still biscuits.

author: Rachel M
subject: Re: Who finished teh emergency biscuits?
body: Reclassified as biscuits. Mystery consumption continues but paperwork reduced.

author: Dale Mercer
subject: Sausage sizzle versus teh grocery list
body: Went out for milk. Returned with sausages eaten and no milk.

author: Jo Underconstruction
subject: Re: Sausage sizzle versus teh grocery list
body: Write teh list down and check it before driving home.

author: Trevor Pike
subject: Re: Sausage sizzle versus the grocery list
body: A sausage sizzle is a compulsory road toll payable in onions.

author: Dale Mercer
subject: Re: Sausage sizzle versus teh grocery list
body: Went back. Bought milk before passing teh onions this time.

author: Tessa Inbox
subject: Weather forecast for an actual clothesline
body: Television says scattered showers. Every shower appears to know where my washing is.

author: Bea IRQ
subject: Re: Weather forecast for an actual clothesline
body: Scattered does not mean evenly distributed across your personal afternoon.

author: Pete Cassette
subject: Re: Weather forecast for an actual clothesline
body: Move teh forecast outside and let it explain itself to teh sheets.

author: Tessa Inbox
subject: Re: Weather forecast for an actual clothesline
body: Sheets inside again. Television has been advised of teh discrepancy.

author: Andy North
subject: Neighbour collecting lawn clippings competitively
body: His bin is always fuller. I suspect he is importing grass.

author: Mo Exchange
subject: Re: Neighbour collecting lawn clippings competitively
body: You do not have to make garden waste into a competition.

author: Lance Frames
subject: Re: Neighbour collecting lawn clippings competitively
body: Borrow his mower and see whether teh score changes.

author: Andy North
subject: Re: Neighbour collecting lawn clippings competitively
body: Have decided to compete on how little mowing I can justify.

author: Ash Jumper
subject: Sunday drive accidentally includes five garden centres
body: Was promised a short outing. Have now inspected more shrubs than roads.

author: Mara Packet
subject: Re: Sunday drive accidentally includes five garden centres
body: Agree teh destination and number of stops before departure.

author: r00tbeer
subject: Re: Sunday drive accidentally includes five garden centres
body: A garden centre is a rest area for peopel who already have too many pots.

author: Ash Jumper
subject: Re: Sunday drive accidentally includes five garden centres
body: Home with two pots. Apparently teh agreement excluded specials.

author: Stan Rook
subject: Family visiting: telephone occupied indefinitely
body: One relative calling anohter to report things teh whole room jsut heard.

author: Denise Carter
subject: Re: Family visiting: telephone occupied indefinitely
body: Agree a call time if others need teh shared line.

author: PacketLord
subject: Re: Family visiting: telephone occupied indefinitely
body: Connect teh room to teh call and finish teh entire family administration at once.

author: Stan Rook
subject: Re: Family visiting: telephone occupied indefinitely
body: We made a list. Calls shorter, conversations in teh room somehow longer.

author: Owen Bundle
subject: Cannot find anyone to feed teh goldfish
body: Weekend away requires a roster approaching a military exercise.

author: Ruth Handshake
subject: Re: Cannot find anyone to feed teh goldfish
body: Arrange a reliable person and clear instructions appropriate to teh fish.

author: Kev Baud
subject: Re: Cannot find anyone to feed the goldfish
body: Ask teh fish whether it would prefer visiting your mother.

author: Owen Bundle
subject: Re: Cannot find anyone to feed teh goldfish
body: Neighbour agreed. Instructions are now shorter than teh weekend.

author: Fern Filename
subject: Why are all picnic blankets damp?
body: Every blanket comes home damp even when it did not rain.

author: Jo Underconstruction
subject: Re: Why are all picnic blankets damp?
body: Dry it fully before folding and storing it.

author: Trevor Pike
subject: Re: Why are all picnic blankets damp?
body: Picnic blankets produce thier own weather when left in boots.

author: Fern Filename
subject: Re: Why are all picnic blankets damp?
body: Dried everything. Car now smells less like a travelling lawn.

author: Mark Ellis
subject: Teh annual battle over teh television aerial
body: One channel clear only when somebody stands in teh wrong place.

author: Bea IRQ
subject: Re: Teh annual battle over teh television aerial
body: Check teh aerial connections and equipment safely; leave roof work to someone equipped for it.

author: Pete Cassette
subject: Re: The annual battle over the television aerial
body: Offer teh helpful person a chair and a long-term viewing contract.

author: Mark Ellis
subject: Re: Teh annual battle over teh television aerial
body: Getting it checked. Brother refusing permanent employment as an indoor transmitter.

author: Graham S
subject: Missing jandal returns on teh wrong foot
body: Found one by teh back door. Other apparently living an independent life.

author: Mo Exchange
subject: Re: Missing jandal returns on teh wrong foot
body: Check teh car and beach bag before accusing teh dog.

author: Lance Frames
subject: Re: Missing jandal returns on the wrong foot
body: Buy two left ones and let economics reunite teh pair.

author: Graham S
subject: Re: Missing jandal returns on teh wrong foot
body: Found behind teh chilly bin. Dog has demanded an apology.

author: Doreen Mills
subject: Three households, one ladder
body: Need the ladder. Owner thinks I have it. Third household says it was never theirs.

author: Mara Packet
subject: Re: Three households, one ladder
body: Start with who last borrowed it and record where it goes next.

author: r00tbeer
subject: Re: Three households, one ladder
body: The ladder has achieved freedom. We should respect its climb to independence.

author: Doreen Mills
subject: Re: Three households, one ladder
body: Found at the fourth house. We have discovered an additional member of the borrowing network.

author: Colin R
subject: Printer says offline while sitting beside me
body: Printer is clearly in the room. Computer refuses to recognise this evidence.

author: Denise Carter
subject: Re: Printer says offline while sitting beside me
body: Check the connection, power and printer queue status rather than its physical proximity.

author: PacketLord
subject: Re: Printer says offline while sitting beside me
body: Introduce them formally. Computers dislike informal arrangements.

author: Colin R
subject: Re: Printer says offline while sitting beside me
body: Queue setting corrected. Social introduction was unnecessary but completed anyway.

author: Nicky Retry
subject: Mouse cable seems to determine cursor range
body: Cannot reach the corner without running out of desk.

author: Ruth Handshake
subject: Re: Mouse cable seems to determine cursor range
body: Lift and reposition the mouse as needed; check the sensitivity settings.

author: Kev Baud
subject: Re: Mouse cable seems to determine cursor range
body: Buy a larger corner. The screen appears to be exceeding the furniture licence.

author: Nicky Retry
subject: Re: Mouse cable seems to determine cursor range
body: Adjusted the sensitivity. Desk no longer under consideration for replacement.

author: Helen Crate
subject: Document opens on the wrong computer
body: Copied a shortcut to a floppy and it will not open elsewhere.

author: Jo Underconstruction
subject: Re: Document opens on the wrong computer
body: Copy the actual document, not just a reference to its location.

author: Trevor Pike
subject: Re: Document opens on the wrong computer
body: A shortcut is a promise made by the original computer, which is not travelling.

author: Helen Crate
subject: Re: Document opens on the wrong computer
body: Copied the real file. It has become larger and more useful.

author: June Ledger
subject: Modem tries to dial the fax machine
body: Saved number apparently belongs to an office fax.

author: Bea IRQ
subject: Re: Modem tries to dial the fax machine
body: Check the exact number and your connection profile before retrying.

author: Pete Cassette
subject: Re: Modem tries to dial the fax machine
body: The fax is answering because it has fewer standards than the provider.

author: June Ledger
subject: Re: Modem tries to dial the fax machine
body: One digit wrong. Fax has declined further conversation.

author: Rachel M
subject: New account password works only when annoyed
body: Typing slowly fails. Angry retry succeeds.

author: Mo Exchange
subject: Re: New account password works only when annoyed
body: Check letter case, keyboard state and what the field actually accepts without exposing the password.

author: Lance Frames
subject: Re: New account password works only when annoyed
body: Maybe the account requires a minimum level of conviction.

author: Rachel M
subject: Re: New account password works only when annoyed
body: Caps Lock identified. Anger has been removed from the login procedure.

author: Dale Mercer
subject: Floppy labelled BACKUP is empty
body: Have kept a backup disk for months. Apparently never put anything on it.

author: Mara Packet
subject: Re: Floppy labelled BACKUP is empty
body: Verify copies actually exist and can be read. A label is not a backup operation.

author: r00tbeer
subject: Re: Floppy labelled BACKUP is empty
body: At least the label is safely stored on the disk.

author: Dale Mercer
subject: Re: Floppy labelled BACKUP is empty
body: Made and checked a real copy. Label now supported by evidence.

author: Tessa Inbox
subject: Installer wants another disk we do not have
body: Installation asks for Disk 3. Box has Disk 1 twice.

author: Denise Carter
subject: Re: Installer wants another disk we do not have
body: Check the complete legitimate installation set rather than guessing with unrelated disks.

author: PacketLord
subject: Re: Installer wants another disk we do not have
body: Put both Disk 1s in the room and wait for arithmetic.

author: Tessa Inbox
subject: Re: Installer wants another disk we do not have
body: Found Disk 3 in the manual. Spare Disk 1 remains a philosophical problem.

author: Andy North
subject: Homepage opens as a wall of HTML
body: Browser is displaying the angle brackets instead of the page.

author: Ruth Handshake
subject: Re: Homepage opens as a wall of HTML
body: Check the file extension and how it is being served. Keep a copy before renaming.

author: Kev Baud
subject: Re: Homepage opens as a wall of HTML
body: The computer has decided to show its working for partial credit.

author: Andy North
subject: Re: Homepage opens as a wall of HTML
body: File had a hidden text extension. Renamed correctly and the page displays.

author: Ash Jumper
subject: Email sent to my printer
body: Address book entry contains an unexpected local destination.

author: Jo Underconstruction
subject: Re: Email sent to my printer
body: Check the selected recipient and application before sending anything else.

author: Trevor Pike
subject: Re: Email sent to my printer
body: Printer has always wanted to feel included in correspondence.

author: Ash Jumper
subject: Re: Email sent to my printer
body: Wrong entry removed. Printer returned to its normal relationship with bills.

author: Stan Rook
subject: Two modems share one cable badly
body: Trying to give two modems the same serial connection with an adapter.

author: Bea IRQ
subject: Re: Two modems share one cable badly
body: Check the supported connection arrangement; a physical splitter does not create independent serial ports.

author: Pete Cassette
subject: Re: Two modems share one cable badly
body: Perhaps they could take alternate letters.

author: Stan Rook
subject: Re: Two modems share one cable badly
body: Using a supported separate-port setup. Alternate letters would have made quoting difficult.

author: Owen Bundle
subject: Disk full despite deleting a desktop icon
body: Removed the picture of the program. Space unchanged.

author: Mo Exchange
subject: Re: Disk full despite deleting a desktop icon
body: An icon or shortcut is not necessarily the program itself. Use the appropriate uninstall process.

author: Lance Frames
subject: Re: Disk full despite deleting a desktop icon
body: You removed its public relations department, not its headquarters.

author: Owen Bundle
subject: Re: Disk full despite deleting a desktop icon
body: Uninstalled properly. Freed space without further symbolic gestures.

author: Fern Filename
subject: Web page wants a newer browser every week
body: At what point do I get to read the page rather than service the browser?

author: Mara Packet
subject: Re: Web page wants a newer browser every week
body: Check whether there is a simpler version and whether the upgrade suits your machine.

author: r00tbeer
subject: Re: Web page wants a newer browser every week
body: My upgrade is to read a different page.

author: Fern Filename
subject: Re: Web page wants a newer browser every week
body: Found a text version. Considerably less exciting, considerably more readable.

author: Mark Ellis
subject: Sound stops when the telephone rings
body: Only the PC speakers go quiet. Modem remains connected.

author: Denise Carter
subject: Re: Sound stops when the telephone rings
body: Note which applications and devices are involved and test one change at a time.

author: PacketLord
subject: Re: Sound stops when the telephone rings
body: Computer is observing a respectful silence for the incoming call.

author: Mark Ellis
subject: Re: Sound stops when the telephone rings
body: Tracked it to a local setting. Telephone no longer controls the soundtrack.

author: Graham S
subject: Cannot tell which desktop icon is the Internet
body: Three browsers, two connection icons and a picture of the Earth.

author: Ruth Handshake
subject: Re: Cannot tell which desktop icon is the Internet
body: Separate the dial-up connection from the program you use after connecting.

author: Kev Baud
subject: Re: Cannot tell which desktop icon is the Internet
body: The one most recently installed will claim ownership of all the others.

author: Graham S
subject: Re: Cannot tell which desktop icon is the Internet
body: Renamed the shortcuts clearly. The Earth still refuses to identify its department.

author: Doreen Mills
subject: Saved page has vanished into another folder
body: Save dialog went somewhere different and I accepted it confidently.

author: Jo Underconstruction
subject: Re: Saved page has vanished into another folder
body: Search for the filename and check the last-used save location.

author: Trevor Pike
subject: Re: Saved page has vanished into another folder
body: The document is on holiday in My Documents' less respectable cousin.

author: Doreen Mills
subject: Re: Saved page has vanished into another folder
body: Found it. Now saving into a folder I can identify without a search party.

author: Colin R
subject: Mail client repeatedly asks for the password
body: One account works. Another keeps prompting.

author: Bea IRQ
subject: Re: Mail client repeatedly asks for the password
body: Check that account's username, server settings and exact error. Avoid posting credentials.

author: Pete Cassette
subject: Re: Mail client repeatedly asks for the password

author: Rachel M
subject: The flat telephone constitution, first draft, already disputed
body:
After last month's toll bill we have finally held the meeting everybody
has been avoiding. I wrote an agenda. This was my first mistake, because
we then spent fifteen minutes arguing whether a flat meeting was allowed
to have an agenda without becoming the sort of flat nobody wanted to
live in.

There are five of us. One works nights, one is looking for work, one has
a girlfriend in another town, one has discovered the Internet, and I have
apparently become the Department of Telecommunications because the bill
arrives in my name. It does not follow that I know why the phone company
charged for each call. It particularly does not follow that I can make
charges disappear by being sufficiently stern on the telephone.

Proposal one: a notebook beside the phone. You record toll calls. This
was rejected by the person who said it would be difficult to remember.
I suggested that remembering to pay for something you used might be a
useful adult skill. The meeting briefly moved onto the subject of my tone.
Proposal two: everyone pays an equal share. Rejected by the person with
no distant girlfriend, on the grounds that love should fund itself.
Proposal three: the person making the call pays for it. Accepted until
we reached the question of calls made for the benefit of the whole flat.

Apparently ordering pizza, ringing the landlord and asking somebody's
mother how to remove a stain are collective acts. Asking about a party
may be collective, depending on whether everyone is invited. Ringing a
job advertisement is an investment in future flat solvency, although
nobody has offered to share any resulting salary. We had not yet reached
the Internet when somebody announced that the oven was on.

So here is the draft: basic shared costs from the kitty; identifiable
personal toll calls paid by the caller; a note beside the phone; advance
agreement for long sessions on the line; necessary calls take priority,
with necessary defined by something other than the caller's enthusiasm.
No one is to unplug anybody else's connection as a negotiation tactic.

If your flat has a working system, I would like to hear it. If your
suggestion is that all five of us obtain separate houses and telephones,
please include the money with your reply. We have already considered
that option at considerable length and no practical depth.

since several of you have suggested my previous report was light on

first, the desk had to move. the desk had been assembled in a position
from which it could apparently never leave. behind it were a dead pen,
three leads i had been blaming somebody else for losing, and enough dust
to require its own property assessment. the installer was polite about

to tell their colleagues.

then we established that where i wanted the equipment and where it was
sensible to put the cable were not the same place. i had drawn a plan.
the plan did not include walls, access or the fact that the wardrobe was
fixed. i now understand why buildings are usually drawn before networks.
we agreed on a route which i described to the flat as temporary. nobody
believed this because they have seen my other temporary cables.

once it was working i fetched several familiar pages. they were much
quicker. i then timed one without considering whether the browser had
already stored it, posted an extremely confident number, and was invited
to learn what a cache was by six people simultaneously. i did know what
a cache was. i had simply hoped it would not become relevant in public.

proper comparisons are less cinematic. use the same actual transfer,
check that it really came over the connection, measure a useful interval,
and write down what else the machine and link were doing. tiny files
finish before the display tells a useful story. a remote server can be
the slow part. the computer can spend time doing things which are not
downloading. none of this makes the connection bad, but it does make my
original description of infinite speed difficult to defend.

what has actually changed is that using the connection is no longer a
household ceremony. i do not have to arrange an opening in the telephone
schedule to read one message. that is the benefit i notice most. i have
also spent a distressing amount of time reading arguments i previously
would have disconnected before finishing. progress has hidden costs.

this is not an apology for enjoying it. it is an apology for the bitmap.
i have looked at the size of the bitmap. even i can see the point now.

author: Andy North
subject: Games night post-mortem: seven computers, very little Quake
body:
I said I would write this up because the next person organising a games
night deserves a chance to make different mistakes.

We invited six people and assumed everybody knew what to bring. This
produced seven computers, five monitors, several bags described as all
the necessary cables, and one person who thought he was coming to play
on somebody else's machine. The person with the extra computer had no
keyboard for it. Naturally that was the machine he regarded as essential.
The first hour was spent borrowing parts from machines which then became
the next machines requiring borrowed parts.

The software was not as uniform as the invitations. People had different
versions, different settings and different ideas about what already
installed meant. In one case it meant a directory copied from a machine
no longer in the room. We should have checked the supported game versions
and a working setup in advance, not assumed six individual successes
would combine into a seventh and much larger success.

By the time we had a consistent arrangement, the discussion had become
competitive. The cable owner announced that he was accustomed to better
latency. The T3 owner established that he did not actually own a T3 but
had access to a computer near one. Somebody reported a very good ping to
a machine which was not participating. None of these contributions
identified the missing lead.

Eventually we played. One computer was visibly struggling locally, which
is not the same problem as network delay. One player complained about
lag immediately after walking into lava without another player present.
Two players knew the map, which turned out to be an unfair advantage
according to people who had spent the setup period explaining networking
instead of looking at the map. I include myself in that last category.

Next time: agree the versions and connection method; test an actual pair
of machines first; make a written equipment list; arrange safe power and
cable placement; choose a setup deadline after which we stop adding new
hardware; and have something enjoyable to do if it all fails. Also food.
Food must not depend on the machine currently being used as a print server.

We did have fun. We would have had more fun if we had not defined success
as proving that all seven machines could be made to work simultaneously.
The evening was rescued by people lending things and being patient, not
by the person repeatedly telling us that it worked at his place.

author: Jo Underconstruction
subject: A page that works before the background arrives
body:
Several people asked what I meant by a small usable homepage, so here is
the practical version rather than another round of browser accusations.

Start with the reason somebody came. If the page is about your computer
collection, say what is in the collection and give links to the details.
If it contains a club's meeting time, put the time, place and contact
information in ordinary text. A visitor should not need to download a
picture of your heading to find out whether they have the right page.

Give links names which make sense without the surrounding layout.
"Photos of the restoration" tells me more than three separate links all
called "here". A link to a large file can say what it is and roughly how
large it is. That lets a dial-up visitor decide whether to fetch it now
rather than discovering its size after committing the household phone line.
Check those links after uploading, including their spelling and case.

Keep original pictures separately. Make a smaller copy for the page and
compare its actual size and appearance. A photograph does not need to be
as wide as your entire desktop to demonstrate that a computer exists.
A tiny flat-colour logo and a photograph may suit different formats.
Changing the display dimensions in HTML is not the same as reducing the
file you send. Test what happens when images are not available at all.

Then try the page in a narrow window and, if possible, another browser.
The objective is not to make every browser draw precisely the same
rectangle. It is to leave the contents and navigation usable when a
particular decoration is missing. Ordinary text links as an alternative
to elaborate navigation cost very little. They do not insult the work
you put into the elaborate version; they help somebody reach that work.

Finally, upload the actual files, visit the actual public address and
check it from there. Your local copy may forgive mistakes the server
does not. Keep a copy of the working page before experimenting. It is
much easier to discover what changed when you have something to compare.

You can still have a silly GIF. I am not organising a police force
against silly GIFs. I am merely suggesting that visitors should be able
to find the content while the silly GIF is arranging its entrance.

author: Mara Packet
subject: How a simple support question became a biography of teh modem
body:
Here is what happened in a recent conversation, with teh identifying
details left out becuase I am not trying to restart teh argument.
Somebody said a download was slow. Within three replies they had been
told to replace teh modem, change the browser, change the phone company
and stop expecting miracles from an old computer. Nobody had asked how
slow it was, what was being downloaded or whether it happened every time.

The owner then supplied a complete history of the machine. That was
understandable, because everybody was confidently diagnosing a different
part of it. We acquired its purchase date, former operating system,
previous owner's opinion and the fact that somebody's nephew had once
called the modem a good one. We still did not have an elapsed time and
a byte count. The thread had become very informative about the family
and not particularly informative about the transfer.

A useful report can start much smaller. What did you try? What happened?
What exact message appeared? Does the problem repeat? What changed before
it began? If it is a speed question, measure a complete transfer and
identify what you measured. If it is a connection problem, distinguish
not connecting from connecting and then failing to deliver data. If the
screen is displaying an error, its words are more useful than the theory
that the computer has taken a dislike to you.

Replying also requires some restraint. Ask one useful question instead
of issuing six unrelated changes. Explain what a proposed test would
separate. Let the owner finish the test before declaring the result.
Keep a working setup or notes so a failed experiment can be undone.
When somebody reports that a suggestion did not help, that is evidence,
not an insult to the person who suggested it.

There is room for humour. Half this group runs on humour. But a joke
followed by an actual question is different from twelve people competing
to tell the owner that the machine is ancient. Some owners already know.
Some owners cannot replace it. Some faults would survive the replacement
because the proposed diagnosis was never tested in the first place.

The final answer in this particular case was a second transfer using
the connection in the background. No new modem was needed. We had spent
more time arguing about possible purchases than it took to establish
what else was running. Make of that what you will.

subject: Weekend away: a complete audit of what we forgot
body:
We have returned from the weekend at the bach. I am posting the inventory
because it may help another household avoid confusing packing thoroughly
with packing usefully.

We took three torches. Two had no batteries. The third had batteries of
uncertain age and produced enough light to confirm that the first two
were still not working. We also took a packet of batteries which fitted
none of the torches. This was described as bad luck rather than a planning
failure by the person who packed them. He had, however, remembered the
battery-powered radio, which provided excellent commentary on the weather
we could already see through the window.

There were four towels, all reserved by their owners for a different
purpose. Nobody would use a beach towel after a shower, or a shower towel
at the beach, or the good towel for anything that might make it wet.
The resulting negotiations took longer than the drive to the nearest
shop. We bought another towel. It has no history and is therefore the
most useful towel in the house.

The food planning assumed sunshine. The weather planning consisted of
hoping for sunshine. We had barbecue supplies, a very small frying pan
and several suggestions that the rain would stop shortly. Once it
became clear that shortly was not an actual cooking time, we organised
a perfectly good meal indoors. This required abandoning the original
meal plan, which was harder for some people than the original plan had
been to write on the back of an envelope.

Nobody remembered the address of the people who were going to meet us.
Everybody remembered that somebody else had it. The telephone number was
in a notebook at home because we had agreed not to carry too much stuff.
The notebook's absence was particularly impressive given the number of
other objects we had brought on the off chance that they might be useful.

Despite this, it was a good weekend. We walked, read, played cards and
had several conversations which were not about whether the modem was
occupying the telephone. Coming home took longer because we packed the
car in a way which prevented access to the road map, then pretended to
know the route. Next time I am making a list of things to check, rather
than simply a list of things to put in bags.

The new towel is staying with me. It has earned somebody competent.

subject: Project map: running the original modem DSP firmware
body:
This group records work on the modem-dsp-emu project. The investigation
includes the ADSP firmware, the surrounding Eicon card model, native
B-channel transport and the eventual PPP path. It is not enough to make
the handshake look plausible: samples, state, frames and delivered bytes
need separate checks.

These entries summarise the repository's recorded findings. Dates identify
the experiments being described; publishing a summary is not a new test.
Some entries preserve an unsuccessful hypothesis because it explains why
we should not spend another afternoon testing the same wrong thing.

Source: modem-dsp-emu/docs/handoff.md; git log through 7375b8a

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: 23 Oct: V.34 reached data mode; T401 was killing the link
body:
The V.34 19200 loopback reached TrnProgress 0x00d0 on both ends, then
failed with a V.42 FRMR. The timer counted datapump datagrams: 1200 at
2400 datagrams/s meant 500 ms, shorter than the measured 692-743 ms RTT.

A premature SABME retransmission made the answerer re-establish LAPM and
reset its send state. An acknowledgement from before that reset then
looked invalid. The link was obeying the protocol; our timeout was wrong.

Changing the default to 3600 datagrams gives 1.5 s at that rate. The
recorded loopback established CHAP/IPCP and returned 20/20 pings, with
zero FCS errors or link resets. This result is an emulated loopback,
not a qualification of the physical card or a real analogue line.

Source: modem-dsp-emu/docs/v34_data_mode_t401_20261023.md

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: Correction: RXSAMPLE was not unwritten; the observation was misleading
body:
An earlier conclusion said the analogue receive sample array was never
filled. The later execution/write watches contradicted that conclusion.
The overlay itself copies samples into RXSAMPLE through its receive ring;
the kernel need not directly reference the destination addresses.

A frame-boundary snapshot was not sufficient evidence that writes never
occurred during the frame. The proposed replacement receive path would
have replaced something already working.

The physical follow-up recorded 4096 isolated routine calls matching
hardware for the V8.ANA biquad, magnitude and detector paths, including
history and counters. That establishes those tested routines, not the
correctness of complete live-call scheduling.

Source: modem-dsp-emu/docs/analog_rxsample_correction.md

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: 24 Oct: continuous SPORT1 transport is not yet lossless transport
body:
Three saved 60-second hardware ring runs had no overruns or underruns
and retained a one-sample loop delay. They still contained 25-41 sample
anomalies per run. In the final run, all 36 were zero substitutions and
remained wrong on reread.

The old word "clean" had meant flow continuity. The runner now separates
flow_continuous from anomaly_free, and successful clean status requires
both. A stream can keep moving at the right rate while carrying wrong
words. Treating those as the same result hid the next investigation.

Source: modem-dsp-emu/docs/sport_ring_status_20261024.md

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: Isolation controls point back at board receive configuration
body:
The recorded controls on the spare board included faster host polling,
a second DSP, autonomous TX, constant IPAC DU input and runs without live
host IDMA. The zeros did not disappear. An RX-only autonomous DMA control
captured one unexpected zero among 8192 retained words in two of three
trials; the third was exact.

The supported next target is receive clock/framing/DU configuration.
These observations do not justify changing emulator arithmetic or host
scheduling merely to hide the substituted samples. Stock firmware was
restored after the bounded hardware controls.

Source: modem-dsp-emu/docs/handoff.md, 24 Oct SPORT1 isolation summary; docs/sport_ring_status_20261024.md

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: 9 Oct result: a codec-law descriptor error kept V.90 off-grid
body:
The direct backend had not set the PCMU channel-descriptor law word.
The V.90 digital firmware consequently ran an A-law configuration on a
mu-law line. The recorded downstream constellation was off-grid, with
12.9 percent BER.

Setting the law through configure_g711_law() and adding V.90 mailbox
support allowed PPP/IPCP and 8/8 pings through that loopback. The recorded
downstream BER fell to 0.15 percent at 38666 bit/s. A retrain about 28 s
into data mode still dropped the link. This was progress, not a clean
long-duration V.90 qualification.

Source: modem-dsp-emu/docs/handoff.md, 9 Oct IP follow-up; docs/v90a_live_caller_capture.md

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: 4 Nov: the shared PTY slave was the wrong suspect
body:
The live PPP investigation had already demonstrated the framing against
a real pppd, as well as the bearer and intermediate hops. The remaining
failure was intermittent and affected traffic in both directions.

A diagnostic released and retook the permanent PTY slave hold across two
live calls. It behaved as intended, but moved no PPP frames either way.
That disproved the proposed shared-slave ownership explanation for those
runs. The next inspection point in the recorded investigation was the
DTE ring and dte_payload() path, not another variation on tty ownership.

Source: modem-dsp-emu commit 7375b8a; docs/mlppp_7910_20261104.md, shared-slave investigation

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: 4 Nov: aggregation worked, useful throughput still did not
body:
The hardware ISP work needs its own result boundary. Two connected
members did carry data, including a measured mixed-card interval with
almost equal transmitted MP frame volume on both channels. Useful TCP
goodput was still poor and retransmission/stalls remained.

The full-framing experiment disabled protocol/address-control compression
and the logs confirmed the client removed those options. That did not
prevent the later stall. A secondary CONNECT light and a joined bundle
are not substitutes for sustained receiver-side delivery measurements.
No specific remaining cause was established by that compatibility test.

Source: modem-dsp-emu/docs/mlppp_7910_20261104.md, mixed-card and full-framing observations

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: Project map: a SIP/G.711 softmodem, not an audio effect
body:
The main role is the digital side of V.90/V.92: an analogue modem calls
through an FXS path, while the softmodem trains over SIP/RTP and hands
data to a PTY. G.711 codewords represent the digital DS0 path; they are
not merely a recording of modem noises.

The project also contains other modem families, clear channel and fax.
Coverage varies by mode and peer. The readme's status matrix distinguishes
engine-pair tests, firmware emulation and actual hardware calls instead
of presenting one broad "supported" badge.

These are summaries of the real development notes, separate from the
fictional conversations elsewhere on this news server.

Source: v90modem/readme.md; docs/README.md

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: Design boundary: preserve digital G.711 codewords exactly
body:
On the digital side, the RTP payload is the DS0 presented to the network
D/A. Resampling, speech enhancement, gain changes or decode/re-encode
operations can destroy the codeword relationship a PCM modem needs.

That is distinct from the analogue role's linear-PCM interface. Its
16 kHz audio timeline represents half-symbol timing and calibrated
headroom; it is not permission to change digital-side G.711 words.
Sample accounting is a protocol concern, not just an audio-quality knob.

Source: v90modem/AGENTS.md, modem constraints; docs/v92_full_startup.md, endpoint interfaces

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: 8 Oct hardware milestone: more than CONNECT and a screenshot
body:
The recorded Eicon V.90 analogue-caller work includes two roughly
26.5-minute calls and 16177152 checked payload bytes with no sequence,
CRC or payload errors. Both codec laws passed PPP with 30/30 pings and
exact 1 MiB HTTP transfers.

The readme reports about 6.44 kB/s binary and 6.21 kB/s HTTP on that LAN
path with a 40 ms jitter buffer. Those measurements describe that rig
and those calls. They do not qualify every modem or remove the separate
open work in the digital answerer's upstream receiver.

Source: v90modem/readme.md, hardware headline result; docs/eicon_soak_ppp.md

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: 28 Oct: the equaliser gradient was in the wrong coordinates
body:
The MT9234 upstream receiver trained, then lost decoding and fell back.
The equaliser error was measured after carrier derotation, but the old
NLMS update multiplied it directly against raw input coordinates.

Returning the error through the inverse rotation fixes the coordinate
mismatch. The same-symbol phase matters: use the phase that derotated
that sample, before the carrier update advances it. The DD and CMA
branches share the corrected transformation.

The retained replay still contains acquisition damage. The correction
reduced damaged segments and final symbol error; it did not magically
turn the original recording into a zero-error capture.

Source: v90modem/docs/mt9234_v90_gradient.md

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: MT9234 physical follow-up: bounded payload, bounded claim
body:
The corrected physical calls held V.90/LAPM/V42bis for the requested
60 seconds without retrains or renegotiations. The second call negotiated
46666 down / 26400 up and delivered a known 1920-byte upstream payload
byte-for-byte to the answerer.

The first corrected call reported zero TX/RX frame errors; the second
reported one TX frame error and zero RX frame errors. Those are the
recorded diagnostics, not a claim that both calls were error-free.
Longer multi-peer qualification remains a different task.

Source: v90modem/docs/mt9234_v90_gradient.md, physical confirmation

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: 5 Nov: the 37333 upstream collapse was in our receive decisions
body:
The same live decoder-input capture produced 248957 wrong bits out of
3447416 with the old frame-local decoder. A continuous-trellis prototype
with about 6 ms lookahead produced zero on that compared input.

The old receiver retained only one winning end state after each short
frame. Discarding the other trellis alternatives could poison the next
frame's starting decision. Zero rejected-frame counts did not imply zero
BER: wrong outputs could still belong to the valid source alphabet.

This initial replay established a receive limitation. By itself it was
not a higher-rate live interoperability pass.

Source: v90modem/docs/v92_upstream_trellis.md, diagnosis and controlled experiment

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: Streaming trellis integration: retain alternatives across frames
body:
The production receiver now retains all 16 trellis state metrics across
frame boundaries. A bounded survivor ring provides 48 symbols, or 6 ms,
of decision lookahead. That delay is an implementation choice, not a
new delay requirement imposed on the peer.

Delayed decisions must update the equaliser rows belonging to the earlier
input frame. Decoder delay is not a licence to add or remove samples.
The regression fixture requires 279776 guarded bits with zero errors
under input chunks of 1, 37, 160 and 320 samples. The old decoder made
13637 errors on that fixture's guarded bits.

Source: v90modem/docs/v92_upstream_trellis.md, production receiver and regressions

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: Wired qualification: hashes beat nominal upstream rates
body:
The subsequent wired slmodemd campaign recorded 11 passing calls and
6029312 receiver-verified bytes in each direction, with complete hashes
acknowledged. Long 37333 and 38666 upstream calls passed 1 MiB each way.

The 37333 long-call upload goodput was about 33.983 kbit/s; the 38666
long call delivered about 34.344 kbit/s. Nominal 40000/41333 calls passed
smaller transfers but were not faster. A clean 42666 repeat failed B1u
acquisition. The unforced selector still chose 36000.

These are wired slmodemd results on the documented rig, not qualification
against a physical V.92 modem. Defaults were not raised merely because
some forced higher-rate calls passed.

Source: v90modem/docs/v92_upstream_trellis.md, wired slmodemd qualification

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: 22 Oct: turning the spare ADSPs into an instruction oracle
body:
The 4BRI card's DSPs are reached through the board MIPS, not the PRI-only
host access path. A small bare-metal MIPS loader follows the stock
protocol's reset and IDMA sequence, installs a test program and reads
results back. This makes single-instruction comparisons possible on the
actual ADSP-2181s rather than treating another emulator as ground truth.
The first run exposed two heavily used instruction behaviours in ours.

Source: modem-dsp-emu/docs/dsp_conformance_20261022.md

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: Hardware comparison: saturated ALU results and status flags
body:
One conformance finding concerned AZ/AN with AR saturation enabled.
The emulator derived those flags from the overflowed intermediate sum;
the hardware result establishes the saturated value as the relevant
basis. Testing AR alone would have missed an instruction that returned
the right visible value but left the wrong branch conditions.
The bench records status as well as arithmetic output.

Source: modem-dsp-emu/docs/dsp_conformance_20261022.md, AR_SAT flags

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: 14 Oct: add-with-carry overflow had a modem-level consequence
body:
The old helpers folded carry into Y before checking signed overflow.
At a sign boundary that could report overflow for a valid signed sum,
and saturation could then turn 0x7fff into 0x8000. Overflow now uses the
original operands while carry-out uses the complete unsigned sum.
With this correction the firmware pair carried PPP at 21600, 26400 and
negotiated 31200 bit/s; the unrestricted control checked a 64 KiB TCP file.
These were local emulated results with normal quality controls retained.

Source: modem-dsp-emu/docs/v34_adc_20261014.md

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: 14 Oct: the 33600 acceptance run checked the file at the receiver
body:
The mixed Analog 109 / PRI 117 pair held DATA for over 558 DSP seconds,
transferred 1310720 bytes on one TCP connection and matched source and
receiver SHA-256. All 100 pings returned; the recorded run had no retrain,
PPP FCS error, link reset or substituted/dropped receive sample.
Both mailboxes published 14-bit datagrams at 2400 Hz.
This is a local emulated loopback, not a physical-line benchmark.

Source: modem-dsp-emu/docs/v34_33600_20261014.md

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: The send loop was adding its own work to every packet period
body:
Sleeping a whole packet interval after sending made send work accumulate
into the clock period. Waiting for the absolute next-send deadline avoids
that drift. The deterministic example is a 6 ms send cost inside a 20 ms
period: wait 14 ms, not another 20. An overdue empty queue still backs off.
This change and the smaller V.34 cushion reduced the measured delay enough
for the firmware's own rate control to retain 3429 symbols/s.
The firmware delay threshold itself was not patched out.

Source: modem-dsp-emu/docs/v34_33600_20261014.md, wire clock

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: 23 Oct: original ANSam generator agrees across all eight DSPs
body:
The original V8.ANA routine generated 7680 samples on each physical DSP.
All 61440 samples and the captured final state matched the emulator.
The measured tone was 2100 Hz with the expected phase-reversal behaviour.
A derived segment also travelled exactly through the physical SPORT/IPAC
loop. Generation parity and a finite loop segment remain distinct from
a lossless, continuously serviced live modem path.

Source: modem-dsp-emu/docs/modem_tone_output_20261023.md

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: More than one sine wave: V.21 generator payload checks
body:
The same overlay's seven modulation tones and full V.21 FSK generator
were compared on all eight physical DSPs. All 38400 recorded samples
matched the emulator, and the 300 bit/s FSK output demodulated with zero
bit errors in the documented test. These isolated runs had no BRI line,
SPORT clock or analogue connection. They test the generator routines,
not complete call establishment across a real telephone circuit.

Source: modem-dsp-emu/docs/modulation_tone_generators_20261023.md

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: 23 Oct measurement corrected the PCI bandwidth intuition
body:
A 20 ms media block cost 97 microseconds of MMIO on the stopped spare:
about 0.5 percent duty. The measured word-at-a-time rate also exceeded
one channel's 8000 words/s by a large margin. Host access bandwidth was
not the bottleneck the earlier architectural worry had suggested.
That does not solve the frame-rate control plane, nor the later observed
zero substitutions in the continuous ring. Feasibility and correctness
are separate claims.

Source: modem-dsp-emu/docs/mmap_media_ring_scope_20261023.md

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: 13 Oct: native ISDN profiles pass payload and PPP in virtual time
body:
The host-native backend exercised nine fixed profiles, transferring
32768 known bytes each way and answering 100/100 PPP pings per mode.
The clean controls reported no bearer/PPP FCS errors or retransmitted
I frames. That backend implements the bearer protocols itself; it is
not evidence that closed firmware executed those same data paths.
The clock was deterministic simulated bearer time, not measured realtime
hardware throughput. Several signalling and negotiation features remain
outside the fixed-profile subset.

Source: modem-dsp-emu/docs/isdn_native_20261013.md

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: N_DATA accepted is not N_DATA received
body:
The original MIPS firmware probes reached native call setup and accepted
a 256-byte N_DATA request after the simulated network CONNECT path was
corrected. The firmware owned the state transitions; the harness supplied
missing network events rather than pinning the target state.
An accepted request only establishes that boundary. No remote bearer or
physical peer received the bytes in that probe, and it must not be
reported as an original-firmware end-to-end PPP pass.

Source: modem-dsp-emu/docs/isdn_native_20261013.md, firmware control-plane evidence

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: Board-model milestone: firmware publishes its own ready signatures
body:
The stock reentrant BRI protocol boots eight ADSP cores and publishes
0x4447 on all four controllers. ASSIGN, REMOVE and signalling reallocation
operate on the separate queues with interrupts enabled. The model does
not synthesise the ready signature, entity ID or IDI success code.
The board-model note also records bearer progress, including native
HDLC/X.75 and bounded modem transfers. It explicitly stops short of
claiming a complete PCI/ISDN replacement.

Source: modem-dsp-emu/docs/bri_card_model.md

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: QEMU frontend: an unmodified guest driver is a useful boundary test
body:
The PCI frontend forwards register operations into the existing board
model instead of returning canned protocol responses. A Linux 4.9 guest
with the unmodified Debian Diva driver bound the device, read the serial,
registered the IRQ and exposed four controller entries. Legacy loading
also wrote firmware through the virtual BAR and executed RESET/START.
Those checks extend beyond a hand-written host probe, but guest attachment
still does not establish every physical ISDN behaviour.

Source: modem-dsp-emu/qemu/README.md

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: 20 Oct audit: acknowledged bytes were lost after LAPM
body:
Six drain sites read bytes out of the RX ring and ignored how many the
PTY actually accepted. A short write therefore discarded the remainder.
LAPM had already acknowledged those bytes; line retransmission could not
recover them. The replacement drain peeks, writes and consumes only the
accepted count. In the recorded six-second DTE-stall regression, the old
path delivered only 1039 bytes of a 12.5 KB payload; the corrected path
retained the complete payload.

Source: v90modem/docs/v42_reliability.md

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: Receiver busy needs to reach the peer before the ring overflows
body:
A slow DTE can be overwhelmed even when the line is error controlled,
especially when compression expands incoming data. Merely setting a
local busy flag did not send the required RNR. The updated data stack
watches available RX room, signals busy early and sends RR or REJ when
clearing it as appropriate. Negative controls lost hundreds of thousands
of bytes in slow-DTE rows; the recorded flow-controlled rows lost none.

Source: v90modem/docs/v42_reliability.md, receiver-busy flow control

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: Queues belong to calls, not the lifetime of the server process
body:
The engine's rings used to initialise only at process startup. Bytes
left by one call could consequently be transmitted on, or delivered from,
the next. Disconnect now permits a bounded drain and then clears the
rings, logging any remaining losses. This is separate from a temporary
retrain on an established call: disconnect cleanup and recovery within
the same call must not be confused.

Source: v90modem/docs/v42_reliability.md, per-call rings

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: Fixing a lossy drain exposed training junk it had been hiding
body:
Once short PTY writes stopped dropping data, training-time V.14 output
became visible after CONNECT. The old bug had accidentally concealed it.
The receive ring is now cleared at the transition into online data and
in data-stack preparation. The reliability audit also added LAPM frame
length/address validation and stopped ignoring a received FRMR.
A fix exposing another defect is not evidence that dropping the data
was correct behaviour.

Source: v90modem/docs/v42_reliability.md, training junk and frame validation

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: MNP is a real fallback path, not a synonym for no error control
body:
The project implements MNP classes 2-4 as the alternative procedure from
V.42 Annex A. The factory path can try MNP when LAPM detection does not
find a peer, before falling back to buffered V.14 where permitted.
Required and forbidden error-control modes still constrain that choice.
MNP5 compression is a separate proprietary negotiation extension; it is
not specified by V.42 merely because MNP error control appears there.

Source: v90modem/docs/mnp.md, protocol source and mode selection

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: MNP5 independent vectors: exact wire bytes, not self-roundtrip only
body:
The retained reference fixture has 284 segments and 73080 plaintext bytes
from execution of the original HSF encoder, checked with its decoder.
It covers byte values, run-length boundaries, rescaling, flushes and
persistent dictionaries. The tests compare encoded wire bytes and decode
fragmented input. A codec agreeing with itself is not as strong a check
as agreement with an independent implementation.
The note explicitly does not count the timed-out macOS ASan run as a pass.

Source: v90modem/docs/mnp.md, independent reference and tests

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: 1 Nov MNP5: a bounded pass did not cure the insertion problem
body:
One 120-second capped hardware call verified 430080 downstream and 98304
upstream DTE bytes, while modem diagnostics still recorded recovered frame
errors and a retrain. A repetition inserted an extra byte after 311296
downstream bytes. Independent HSF decoding checked our emitted LT prefix
across that position. The note therefore claims bounded hardware traffic,
not a reliable insertion workaround or long-hold qualification.

Source: v90modem/docs/mnp.md, MT9234 V.90/MNP5 hardware follow-up

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: V.42bis reset must use the old escape value before replacing state
body:
Compression state persists across arbitrary input boundaries. The stream
implementation negotiates dictionary/string limits and manages transparent
versus compressed mode rather than treating each API call as a new block.
The documented reset sequence flushes pending data, sends ETM where
needed and RESET using the old escape value, then initialises the encoder.
The data-stack compression offer is also distinct from enabling a codec
on a bare V.42 library caller.

Source: v90modem/docs/v42bis.md

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: V.44 selection is explicit, and refusal falls back to plain LAPM
body:
The C data stack has a streaming V.44 implementation ported from the
Python project. Production does not need a Python interpreter. Selecting
V.44 offers that codec with its documented limits; a peer which does not
agree falls back to plain LAPM, not silently to a different compression
algorithm. Bare V.42 API users must attach their own codecs before enabling
the compression offer. Configuration and negotiation are both part of
the result, not just whether a codec function exists.

Source: v90modem/docs/v44.md

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: A 30 ms carrier dip should not necessarily end a call
body:
A CX93001 peer briefly dropped signal during V.22bis/MNP calls. Our
callback hung up on the first carrier-down report, while a receiver
restart also disturbed both directions. The carrier-loss work distinguishes
a temporary loss from the S10 hold interval. The project documents its
factory 1.4-second value and its explicit interpretation of 255; those
are implementation choices, not a default supplied by V.250.

Source: v90modem/docs/carrier_loss.md

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: Stored AT profiles: failure must not half-save configuration
body:
AT&W and AT&Y save through a temporary file and rename. If writing fails,
the command returns ERROR and leaves the in-memory selection unchanged.
ATZ restores the appropriate profile; AT&F is factory configuration only.
Stored dial strings live beside the profiles but are not part of each
profile's reset semantics. Without a profile file, stored configuration
lasts only for the current process. Those distinctions matter when a
test looks correct until restart.

Source: v90modem/docs/at_stored_profiles.md

author: Modem lab notebook
subject: Quick Connect implemented does not mean a foreign peer is qualified
body:
The digital-answering short-startup path has its own G.711 codeword
module and engine integration. The documented +PQC default keeps short
Phase 1/2 disabled because foreign-peer qualification is not established;
+PSS=2 forces full startup. V.92 must also be offered. Implementation
coverage, engine tests and an actual compatible peer are separate gates.
This entry records the interface and qualification boundary, not a new
successful Quick Connect hardware call.

Source: v90modem/docs/v92_quick_connect.md, controls and short Phase 1
